papers.title: Genetic polymorphisms and hypertension in Indian populations: a systematic review and integrative bioinformatics approach.
papers.abstract: Hypertension continues to be a major public health issue in India, with increasing incidence associated with both lifestyle factors and genetic susceptibility. Despite genome-wide association studies identifying several loci related with blood pressure worldwide, there is a paucity of integration of these findings within the genetically varied Indian setting. This systematic review aims to compile current information on single-nucleotide polymorphisms linked to hypertension in Indian communities and to elucidate their biological significance by bioinformatics analysis. Using PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Google Scholar, we conducted a systematic review of studies from 2000 to 2025 following PRISMA guidelines. Two reviewers individually screened and extracted data from studies related to SNPs associated to hypertension in Indians. Study quality was assessed using Q-Genie Tool. Functional and pathway studies have been conducted by SNPnexus, Enrichr, STRING, and GTEx. Twenty-two SNPs across 14 genes were evaluated in Indian cohorts, with several variants showing statistically significant associations with hypertension in at least one included study, particularly within the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone, endothelial nitric oxide, and circadian pathways. Functional annotation identified MTHFR rs1801133 as potentially affecting protein function, while several coding and noncoding variants showed predicted functional or regulatory activity. Pathway analysis highlighted hormonal regulation, vasodilation, and nitric oxide biosynthesis. eQTL analysis showed tissue-specific effects in arteries and vascular cells. This is the first systematic study of Indian hypertension using genetic association data and functional bioinformatics. The findings emphasize the relevance of ancestry-specific genomes and the necessity for large-scale, multi-ethnic investigations to guide Indian hypertension precision therapy.

papers.title: Impact of nurse-led intervention on the level of anxiety and depression among chronic kidney disease patients at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, India.
papers.abstract: Chronic Kidney disease (CKD) patients face ongoing challenges, including lifestyle changes, medication adherence, and managing treatment complexities and complications daily. In a study, it was found the prevalence of anxiety and depression in CKD patients were 28% and 61.3% respectively. The aim was to find out the impact of nurse-led intervention on the level of anxiety and depression among CKD patients. This study was conducted at Tertiary Care Centre from eastern India and focused on CKD patients. The sample consisted of CKD patients (aged over 18 years) who were proficient in Odia, excluding those with existing mental illness or undergoing psychotherapy. Using block randomization with block sizes of 5 and concealed allocation sequences, participants were allocated to either control or an experimental group.The initial sample size was calculated at 60 participants to accommodate potential dropouts during the study period. The nurse-led intervention helped reduce the anxiety levels among CKD patients at different periods, i.e. baseline, 6th week and 12th week of a follow-up visit, which was statistically significant within the group, F(18.594) df-2, p < 0.001 with η2p(0.243), between the group no statistically significance F(2.27) df-1, p = 0.138 with η2p(0.38), Interaction effects between the groups across the time point, F(14.007) df-2, p < 0.001 with η2p(0.07). Nurse-led intervention on depression scores within experimental, between experimental and control groups at different periods, i.e. baseline, 6th week and 12th week of a follow-up visit for CKD patients, which shows a significant effect of time on depression scores (p = 0.05) and a significant overall group difference (p = 0.05). A highly significant time × group interaction (p = 0.001) indicated that depression scores changed differently over time between the experimental and control groups, demonstrating a strong intervention effect. The nurse-led intervention significantly reduces the score of hospital anxiety and depression scale in CKD patients, highlighting the vital role of nursing care in improving mental health, sleep quality and overall wellbeing. The clinical trial was registered with India's Clinical Trial Registry (CTRI/2022/08/044974). Registration Date 26-08-22.

papers.title: Academic-year differences and psychophysiological associations with objective spinal parameters in physiotherapy students: a cross-sectional DIERS formetric 4D study.
papers.abstract: Physiotherapy students are exposed to differing physical and psychological demands across classroom-based and clinical stages of training. Although musculoskeletal symptoms, stress, sleep quality and burnout have been widely investigated in healthcare students, these factors have rarely been examined together using objective three-dimensional spinal assessment. This study compared spinal parameters between third- and fourth-year physiotherapy students and examined their associations with academic-year-related physical exposure, psychophysiological factors, sleep quality, and physical activity. In this cross-sectional study, 132 healthy physiotherapy students (70 third year and 62 fourth year) underwent three-dimensional spinal assessment using the DIERS Formetric 4D system. Trunk length, kyphotic angle and lordotic angle were recorded. Sleep quality, anxiety, burnout and physical activity were evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, State-Trait Anxiety Inventory, Maslach Burnout Inventory and International Physical Activity Questionnaire. Group comparisons were performed, followed by hierarchical multiple linear regression analyses to examine independent associations and bootstrap mediation analyses to explore indirect associations. Multivariable analyses were adjusted for relevant anthropometric, academic-year, school-based standing and sitting, and physical activity variables. Fourth-year students reported longer school-based standing and shorter sitting durations than third-year students (both p < 0.001), alongside lower trait anxiety and burnout scores and higher walking activity. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in trunk length, kyphotic angle, or lordotic angle; kyphotic angle was numerically lower in fourth-year students but did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.051). In the fully adjusted hierarchical model, trait anxiety (β = - 0.148, p = 0.022) and poorer sleep quality (PSQI; β = - 0.139, p = 0.032) were independently associated with shorter trunk length, whereas academic-year group and school-based standing and sitting durations were not. The final model explained 68.4% of trunk-length variance. Exploratory mediation analysis identified a significant indirect association between emotional exhaustion and trunk length through sleep quality (B = - 0.300, 95% bootstrap CI - 0.686 to - 0.062, p = 0.048), while the corresponding direct and total associations were not statistically significant. Objective spinal parameters did not differ significantly between third- and fourth-year physiotherapy students despite marked differences in their school-based standing and sitting exposure. Trunk length was independently associated with trait anxiety and sleep quality after multivariable adjustment, while exploratory analysis identified an indirect association between emotional exhaustion and trunk length through sleep quality. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than temporal or causal relationships. Collectively, the results highlight the potential value of educational strategies that extend beyond ergonomic considerations to integrate biomechanical, psychological, and recovery-related factors during physiotherapy training. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06851780 registered on October 28, 2024.

papers.title: Health and social challenges faced by rare disease patients in Hong Kong: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Literature suggests that rare disease (RD) have adverse effects on patients' physical and psychosocial well-being. RD patients also face various challenges in their daily lives. This study aims to quantify the impact of RDs on patients in Hong Kong in terms of their sociodemographic characteristics, health-related conditions, patient experience, psychosocial support, illness perception, and self-esteem. We conducted a cross-sectional survey of RD patients in Hong Kong. A mixed-mode survey approach, which included purposive, opportunity, and snowball sampling, was adopted. Participants were recruited through Rare Disease Hong Kong (RDHK) and completed a face-to-face, interviewer-administered survey(n = 176). The 127-item survey instrument covered aspects on sociodemographic characteristics, health-related conditions, patient experience, psychosocial support, illness perception, and self-esteem. Health-related quality of life (HRQL) was assessed using 12-item Short-Form Health Survey version 2 (SF-12 v2), from which a Physical Component Summary was derived for physical health, and a Mental Component Summary for psychological health. Univariate analyses and multivariate linear regression analyses were conducted subsequently to examine the associations between HRQL and sample characteristics. RD patients in this study were found to have poor physical and psychological HRQL compared with population norms. They also faced challenges and difficulties in their daily lives, including but not limited to economic activities, ability to work, sleep quality, activities of daily living, patient experience, psychosocial support, outlook on life, and self-esteem. To our knowledge, this is the first study in Hong Kong that quantifies the impact of RDs on patients' HRQL, and their experience throughout the disease journey. Due to the multi-faceted impact of RD on their patients, we opine that it is critical to adopt a capability approach that does not merely emphasize on the resourcist right and entitlement of the patients, but also ensures equality in capabilities in converting resources to outcomes they value by focusing on the social determinants of health beyond healthcare policies.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms underlying loss of functional independence after stroke: EEG evidence of impaired motor-to-sensory directed connectivity on the affected side.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke reorganization of the prefrontal-sensorimotor network is critical for functional recovery, yet single connectivity metrics fail to capture its multidimensional characteristics. This exploratory study investigates network reorganization patterns and their clinical relevance to motor function and daily independence using multimodal electroencephalography (EEG) connectivity analysis, including Coherence (COH), phase lag index (PLI), and Granger causality (GC). Resting-state EEG from stroke patients (n = 22) and healthy controls (n = 22) was analyzed. COH, PLI, and GC metrics were computed for key regional connections involving the prefrontal (PFC), motor (MC), sensory (SC), and parietal (PC) cortices and correlated with Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) and Modified Barthel Index(MBI) scores. For stroke patients, hemispheres were classified as ipsilesional (i, affected) and contralesional (c, unaffected) based on the lesion side. Compared to healthy controls, stroke patients exhibited distinct reorganization patterns. Preliminary evidence suggests enhanced parietal-motor coherence (COH_cPC-cMC↑) in the unaffected hemisphere alongside reduced motor-to-prefrontal directed connectivity (GC_cMC→cPFC↓). Interhemispherically, the findings may indicate weakened information flow from the unaffected to affected motor/sensory areas (GC_cMC→iMC↓, GC_cMC→iSC↓), accompanied by reduced bilateral motor synchronization (PLI_iMC-cMC↓). Within the affected hemisphere, there was evidence of enhanced bidirectional parietal-motor phase transfer (PLI_iPC-iMC↑), whereas directed pathways were significantly impaired (GC_iMC→iSC↓, GC_iPC→iSC↓, GC_iPFC→iMC↓). Clinically, the affected motor-to-sensory pathway (GC_iMC→iSC) showed a strong negative correlation with the MBI (r = -0.61, P = 0.002), and both interhemispheric motor regulation (GC_cMC→iMC) and synchronization (PLI_iMC-cMC) were significantly correlated with functional deficits (P < 0.05). Post-stroke networks may exhibit a "local compensation-global impairment" reorganization pattern. The affected motor-sensory pathway (GC_iMC→iSC) may be a biomarker for functional independence and thus allow for guided sensory integration-based precision rehabilitation.

papers.title: Effects of health promotion behavior education in pregnancy on sleep quality and physical activity: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: This randomized controlled trial was conducted to evaluate the effect of health promotion behavior education for pregnant women on sleep quality and physical activity levels. This randomized controlled trial was conducted with 57 third-trimester pregnant women recruited from a Family Health Center in Türkiye. Participants were randomly assigned to intervention and control groups. The intervention group received six weekly 30-minute face-to-face health promotion education sessions, whereas the control group received routine prenatal care. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, independent samples t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and mixed repeated-measures ANOVA. Because baseline PPAQ total scores differed significantly between groups, additional baseline-adjusted ANCOVA analyses were performed for the post-intervention and one-month follow-up PPAQ total scores. The groups were generally comparable at baseline, although significant differences were observed in pregnancy planning status and baseline PPAQ total scores. No significant difference was found in the household chores and caregiving activities subscale after the intervention and during follow-up. Mixed repeated-measures ANOVA showed no significant group, time, or group × time effect for household/caregiving activities. A significant group and time effect was observed for occupational activity, whereas the group × time interaction approached significance. For sports/exercise activity, the group × time interaction was significant, indicating a more favorable change over time in the intervention group. The education program was found effective in improving exercise/physical behaviors among pregnant women, but showed limited effects on other subdimensions of physical activity. No significant improvement in sleep quality was achieved. Longer-term and multi-component interventions may be more effective in supporting behavioral change among pregnant women. The study was retrospectively registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07315971 first posted 20 November 2025).

papers.title: Sleep patterns and breast cancer risk: a prospective cohort study integrating multi-omics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Sleep is a potentially modifiable behavioural factor that may influence breast cancer risk. This study examined the association between sleep patterns and incident breast cancer in relation to genetic susceptibility and plasma proteomic profiles. This prospective cohort study included 159,452 UK Biobank women free of breast cancer at baseline. Sleep patterns were constructed from five sleep characteristics. Associations with incident breast cancer were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models and time-varying Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, breast cancer-related, and clinical covariates. Kaplan-Meier curves, restricted cubic splines, and PRS-based joint and stratified analyses were performed. In the proteomic subcohort, differential expression, enrichment, and machine-learning-based feature prioritisation analyses were used to identify overlapping proteomic signatures related to sleep pattern and breast cancer status. During follow-up, 7,291 incident breast cancer cases were identified. Compared with a healthy sleep pattern, an unhealthy sleep pattern was associated with a higher risk of breast cancer in the fully adjusted model (HR = 1.10, 95% CI = 1.05-1.15). This association was consistent in time-varying Cox proportional hazards models (HR = 1.34, 95% CI = 1.02-1.77). Joint analyses showed that participants with both high PRS and an unhealthy sleep pattern had the highest breast cancer risk. Proteomic analyses identified overlapping protein signatures related to both sleep pattern and breast cancer status, with enrichment mainly in immune regulation, inflammatory signalling, vascular function, and extracellular matrix-related biological processes. Machine-learning-based feature prioritisation identified CRISP3, PADI2, PLA2G2A, SUSD4, TNFRSF6B, and UPK3A as key candidate proteins. Unhealthy sleep patterns were associated with increased incident breast cancer risk. Integrated genetic and proteomic analyses suggest that immune-inflammatory, vascular, and extracellular matrix-related processes may provide biological context for this association.

papers.title: Sleep bruxism, maximum bite force, and home electromyography: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Sleep bruxism is a sleep-related masticatory muscle activity that may occur during sleep as rhythmic (phasic) or non-rhythmic (tonic) muscle contractions and, in otherwise healthy individuals, is not considered a movement disorder or a sleep disorder. Its relationship with maximum bite force remains unclear. This study aimed to compare maximum bite force between adults with and without sleep bruxism using a combined clinical assessment and multi-night, at-home surface electromyography monitoring. This cross-sectional study enrolled 60 adults aged 18-45 years (30 with sleep bruxism and 30 controls). Sleep bruxism was identified using a multimodal approach that combined self-report, clinical signs, and three nights of at-home single-channel surface electromyography recorded over the masseter muscle with the FLA-500-SD device (GC Corporation, Japan), in accordance with the American Academy of Sleep Medicine criteria. Maximum bite force was measured bilaterally at the first molar, second premolar, and central incisor regions using a digital occlusal force gauge (BFM, 4th generation, Vietnam). Three measurements were conducted per site, and the highest value was used for analysis. Electromyography outcomes included the bruxism episode index (BEI) and the percentage of maximum voluntary contraction (%MVC). Between-group differences were evaluated using the independent-samples t-test or the Mann-Whitney U test (p < 0.05). Maximum bite force at the molar region did not differ between groups, whereas values at the premolar and incisor regions were higher in the sleep bruxism group (p < 0.05). Across all tooth regions, men showed higher maximum bite force than women (p < 0.01). Participants with sleep bruxism exhibited higher maximum bite force in the premolar and incisor regions, while first molar bite force did not differ from controls. These findings may have been influenced by concomitant awake bruxism and should be further investigated in future studies.

papers.title: Association of nocturnal lifestyle with overweight and obesity: a cross-sectional study based on SHOOW (Shanghai Overweight/Obesity and Wellness Study) cohort.
papers.abstract: This study aims to examine the associations between nocturnal lifestyle and overweight/obesity, especially central obesity. While most previous studies have examined individual nocturnal lifestyle factors separately, this study simultaneously evaluates three nocturnal lifestyle behaviors (weekly midnight snack frequency, bedtime, and sleep duration) in a clinical sample of overweight and obese adults, with a specific focus on central obesity indicators. The study was based on clinical data of 1295 overweight and obese patients collected from a weight management outpatient clinic. We analyzed the associations between weekly midnight snack frequency, bedtime, sleep duration and obesity-related indicators. Female patients accounted for 69.19% (896 cases) and male patients accounted for 30.81% (399 cases). Young and middle-aged adults (18-49 years old) constituted the largest proportion, reaching 91.51%. In terms of weekly midnight snack frequency, 58.92% of patients (763 cases) did not consume midnight snacks, 29.96% (388 cases) consumed midnight snacks 1-3 times per week, and 11.12% (144 cases) consumed midnight snacks 4-7 times per week. The largest group of patients (786 cases, 60.70%) went to bed between 22:00 and 24:00, while 409 patients (31.58%) fell asleep between 24:00 and 2:00. Most patients (1111 cases, 85.79%) had a nocturnal sleep duration of 4-8 h. Univariate linear regression analysis showed that weekly midnight snack frequency (4-7 times/week) was significantly positively associated with body mass index (BMI, P = 0.017) and waist circumference (WC, P = 0.003); weekly midnight snack frequency (1-3 times/week) was significantly positively associated with waist-to-hip ratio (WHR, P = 0.009). Compared with the 22:00-24:00 bedtime group, the after 2:00 group was significantly associated with all obesity indicators. The 24:00-2:00 group was significantly associated with all obesity indicators except body fat percentage (BFP). Concerning sleep duration, compared with the 4-8 h group, the > 8 h group was significantly associated with higher BMI (P = 0.002), neck circumference (NC, P = 0.008), WC (P = 0.003), WHR (P = 0.046) and upper arm circumference (UAC, P = 0.008). Multivariate linear regression analysis further confirmed that WC and WHR was jointly associated with weekly midnight snack frequency, bedtime and sleep duration. Nocturnal lifestyle was mainly associated with central obesity indicators, and adjustment of nocturnal lifestyle habits may be a consideration for central obesity prevention efforts.

papers.title: Intermittent Fasting in Metabolic Syndrome: Clinical Evidence, Molecular Mechanisms, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: The objective for this narrative review was to synthesize and critically assess the clinical evidence, molecular mechanisms, and future directions of intermittent fasting (IF) for managing metabolic syndrome (MetS). Metabolic syndrome is a complex cardiometabolic disorder associated with abnormal dietary patterns, epigenetic regulation, and gene activity, and characterized by central adiposity, insulin resistance, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Intermittent fasting regimens, including time-restricted eating, alternate-day fasting, and the 5:2 fasting regimen, are promising nutritional interventions. Nonetheless, large, randomized trials have reported mixed clinical outcomes, and critical uncertainties persist regarding clinical effectiveness, molecular mechanisms, and whether benefits arise from fasting timing or weight-loss-driven energy restriction. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in major databases through July 2026. Articles, including those reporting on randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and relevant preclinical mechanistic investigations in MetS, were selected and their data synthesized. Findings show that certain IF regimens produce modest improvements in body weight, waist circumference, and selected cardiometabolic risk markers; however, effects on glycemic control, lipid profiles, and liver-related end points are heterogeneous across trials. Observed clinical responses vary by fasting protocol, participant phenotype, and adherence, and high-quality human mechanistic data remain limited. Mechanistic insights, largely derived from preclinical models, highlight circadian rhythm synchronization and nutrient-sensing network modulation as key biological pathways. Important unresolved controversies cover protocol optimization, long-term adherence, and inter-individual metabolic variability. Intermittent fasting may serve as a feasible nonpharmacological adjunct intervention for MetS and related conditions, yet existing evidence is inconsistent. Translation toward precision lifestyle medicine requires resolution of ongoing controversies, improved evaluation of evidence quality, development of personalized fasting protocols, and rigorous assessment of long-term safety and sustainability across diverse patient populations.

papers.title: Neural sensitivity to peer rejection predicts depressive symptoms and daily mood in adolescents.
papers.abstract: Understanding the role of peer feedback, particularly rejection, is critical for adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the neurophysiological markers core to peer feedback, especially those that may presage risk for depression, are unclear. Adolescents (N = 179; ages 13-18; healthy controls n = 62, remitted MDD n = 80, current MDD n = 37) completed a baseline clinical assessment and a revised Chatroom Task during EEG recording, from which the P3 to peer acceptance and rejection feedback was quantified. Over 12 months, daily mood and keyboard inputs from adolescents' smartphones were passively obtained. Linear models evaluated whether the P3 difference between rejection and acceptance (ΔP3) prospectively predicted depressive severity and average daily mood. Exploratory natural language processing examined whether friendship-focused social communication moderated the association between neural sensitivity to peer feedback and subsequent clinical outcomes. Group and feedback type interacted in predicting P3 amplitude (F(2176) = 4.84, p = 0.009): adolescents with current MDD showed larger P3 amplitudes to rejection than acceptance, whereas remitted MDD showed elevated amplitudes to both feedback types relative to controls. In a general linear model adjusting for age, sex, site, and baseline depression severity, the Group × ΔP3 interaction was significant in predicting severity at follow-up (b = 0.092, p = 0.045); higher ΔP3 predicted higher follow-up severity in current MDD, but not in remitted MDD or healthy controls. Across the full sample, larger ΔP3 was associated with lower average daily mood over 12 months (b = -1.673, p = 0.045). These findings suggest that enhanced neural sensitivity to peer rejection may be deeply engrained in adolescent depression, shaping both the longitudinal course of depressive symptoms and daily mood.

papers.title: Emerging links between gut dysbiosis, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation, and Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder, is classically defined as a motor disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra and motor dysfunction. Increasing evidence, however, identifies PD as a multisystem disorder with early non-motor features, including sleep, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal disturbances, implicating the gut-brain axis. Tryptophan metabolism through serotonin, kynurenine, and indole pathways generates bioactive metabolites, many of which regulate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). AhR is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic metabolism through canonical signaling pathways; however, growing evidence supports its role in immune balance, glial responses, and barrier integrity. Altered AhR signaling may therefore connect gut dysbiosis and disrupted tryptophan metabolism to sustained, systemic and central inflammation in PD. This review examines gut dysbiosis, tryptophan metabolism, and AhR signaling as potential mechanisms underlying idiopathic PD and highlights their relevance to early diagnosis and disease-modifying therapies.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Seizure Generation and SUDEP in Cortical Dysplasia: A Role for Cortical Up and Down States.
papers.abstract: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP) remains the primary cause of epilepsy-related mortality, yet the preictal brain dynamics that distinguish fatal from nonfatal seizures are not well understood. Identifying the network mechanisms determining these outcomes is critical for developing SUDEP risk biomarkers. Using a neuron-specific PTEN knockout mouse model of cortical dysplasia-which exhibits spontaneous seizures and SUDEP-like events-we employed long-term video-EEG monitoring to analyze cortical state transitions and network signatures. We found that nonfatal seizures are preceded by a progressive "ramp-up" of cortical up and down states, characterized by alternating neuronal depolarization and hyperpolarization, which appears to facilitate seizure initiation. In sharp contrast, sudden death is preceded by a marked suppression of these state transitions and the emergence of infraslow EEG activity, suggestive of spreading depolarizations. This pattern differed from the sustained spike-wave complexes and preserved state transitions observed during status epilepticus. These physiological differences are mirrored behaviorally: nonfatal events typically feature forelimb clonus and spike-wave discharges, whereas fatal seizures are characterized by kicking, tonic hindlimb extension, and diffuse EEG attenuation. Together, these findings suggest that cortical up and down states support seizure initiation, while their disruption and failure to recover postictally predisposes neocortical networks to spreading depression episodes that very likely propagate to brainstem circuits, ultimately triggering SUDEP. By delineating these divergent peri-ictal signatures, this study identifies candidate neurophysiological markers for SUDEP risk stratification.

papers.title: A study protocol of fasting to provide energy needed to help adults in need of cognitive enhancement (Fasting ENHANCE).
papers.abstract: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is defined as a self-perceived reduction in cognitive function and is associated with future cognitive impairment. However, few clinical trials have explored the impact of nonpharmacological interventions in older adults with SCD. Time-restricted eating (TRE) restricts food intake to a daily eating window and has shown improvements in cardiometabolic markers associated with cognitive impairment. The Fasting to provide Energy Needed to Help Adults in Need of Cognitive Enhancement (Fasting ENHANCE) study is a rater-blinded, parallel-group, randomized controlled trial, designed to evaluate the effects of TRE on cognitive function in overweight older adults with SCD. The study aims to enroll older adults (aged ≥65 years) who are overweight (BMI ≥25 kg/m2) and have SCD without objective impairment. Participants are randomized to either a 6-month TRE or Successful Aging (SA) group. The TRE group is instructed to restrict eating to an 8-h window, and the SA group to maintain current lifestyle behaviors. The primary outcome is change in cognitive function, assessed using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status and Montreal Cognitive Assessment at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Secondary outcomes include physical function, blood biomarkers, and self-reported mood, sleep, and quality of life. The Fasting ENHANCE study protocol outlines the methodology for evaluating the effect of TRE on cognitive and metabolic health in older adults with SCD. Results will inform future nonpharmacological interventions aimed at attenuating cognitive decline. ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT05732935.

papers.title: Effects of the Pythagorean Self-Awareness Intervention on total oxidant status and telomere length in breast cancer survivors: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Psychological stress and health behaviors are associated with oxidative status and telomere biology, but evidence from multidomain interventions in breast cancer survivors remains limited. To evaluate the effects of the Pythagorean Self-Awareness Intervention (PSAI) on biological, behavioral, and psychosocial outcomes following breast cancer treatment. In this randomized controlled trial, 120 women were randomized to an eight-week PSAI program or education-only control condition (n = 60 each); 118 were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. Primary biological outcomes were serum total oxidant status and PBMC relative telomere T/S ratio. Linear mixed-effects models estimated group × time effects, between-group differences in change, 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and Hedges' g. Total oxidant status decreased more in the intervention group (difference in change, -3.83 μmol/L; 95% CI -7.03 to -0.63; p = 0.020; g = -0.13). Telomere-length change did not differ significantly between groups (-0.170log₂[T/S] units; 95% CI -0.554 to 0.214; p = 0.382; g = -0.23). PSAI also improved physical activity, body weight, sleep, perceived stress, anxiety, and depression. PSAI improved total oxidant status and several patient-relevant outcomes but did not significantly affect telomere-length change. Longer, adequately powered trials with repeated biomarker assessments are require.

papers.title: An MRI-compatible electrode implantation system for linking behavioral neurophysiology and stimulation-evoked fMRI in non-human primates.
papers.abstract: Local electrophysiology and microstimulation reveal site-specific neural activity and physiological effects but do not directly link these local effects to whole-brain responses from the same target site. We developed an MRI-compatible electrode implantation system for macaques that enables CT/MRI-based localization, postoperative depth adjustment, neural recording, microstimulation during behavioral testing, and subsequent electrical microstimulation combined with functional MRI (EM-fMRI) using the same implanted electrode. The system supported local field potential recording, a stimulation-induced reduction in pupil size, and distributed stimulation-evoked blood oxygenation level-dependent (BOLD) responses. This approach provides a practical framework for linking local neural activity and stimulation-induced physiological responses with whole-brain responses at the same target site.

papers.title: Brain-State-Resolved Consistency of Corticospinal Responses to TMS.
papers.abstract: An important feature of motor-evoked potential (MEP) responses to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) over the primary motor cortex (M1) is their substantial trial-to-trial variability. Ongoing brain activity at the time of TMS, such as the power and phase of the sensorimotor mu rhythm, influences MEP amplitude. It is unclear to what extent these endogenous brain states also shape the consistency of MEP amplitude across trials. We investigated trial-to-trial variability of MEP amplitude as a function of pre-stimulus mu dynamics. Twenty-nine healthy participants received 1200 single TMS pulses over the left M1 during simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) recording; 10 participants completed two sessions to assess inter-session reproducibility. Trials were stratified based on pre-stimulus mu power, phase, and interhemispheric M1-M1 functional connectivity. Brain-state-resolved MEP variability was quantified using the coefficient of variation (CV) within subsets of trials defined by similar pre-stimulus mu dynamics. Trial subsets characterized by high mu power were associated with reduced MEP variability, indicating more consistent corticospinal output. In contrast, mu phase did not significantly influence MEP variability at the group level. Mu power group-level effects were reproducible across sessions in an exploratory test-retest analysis and across experimental sites. We show that inter-trial consistency of MEP amplitude reflects a structured, brain-state-dependent feature of the sensorimotor network. These findings contribute to our mechanistic understanding of trial-to-trial variability in TMS-evoked responses. This may provide a basis for future TMS approaches aimed at reducing response variability and improving the consistency of neuromodulatory effects.

papers.title: Infant Negative Affect During Mother-Infant Interaction Is Associated with Neonatal Limbic-Prefrontal Connectivity in the First Month of Life.
papers.abstract: Early caregiving may shape neonatal limbic circuit organization, yet whether microanalytically coded interaction quality relates to neonatal limbic-prefrontal connectivity is unknown. We tested associations between infant and maternal affect during mother-infant interaction and neonatal limbic-prefrontal cortex (PFC) connectivity. At approximately 30 days postnatal, 143 mother-infant dyads from the Healthy MiNDS cohort (São Paulo, Brazil) completed a video-recorded interaction coded with the Coding Interactive Behavior (CIB) system; infant negative affect was the percentage of interaction time in distress. Neonates underwent resting-state fMRI; limbic-PFC connectivity was quantified by principal component analysis of amygdala and hippocampus seed-to-ROI maps. Covariate-adjusted regressions tested associations. Infant negative affect was associated with right amygdala-PFC (β = -0.247, p = .003) and right hippocampus-PFC connectivity (β = -0.202, p = .021), both surviving FDR correction and robust across multiple analytic approaches. The amygdala association was limited to infant distress-related behaviors, whereas maternal positive expressiveness showed an independent, opposing association (β = 0.202, p = .019); no other CIB measure was significant. Exploratorily, connectivity was associated with sleep problems at 18-24 months in females (r = -.324, p = .030). The emotional quality of early caregiving is associated with neonatal limbic circuit organization: infant distress is selectively associated with weaker amygdala-PFC connectivity, whereas maternal positive affect shows an independent opposing association. These findings identify the mother-infant relationship as a modifiable input to neonatal brain development.
papers.journal: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging

papers.title: Do neuroimaging data have higher-order interactions?
papers.abstract: Recent advances in the physics of complex systems have motivated the study of higher-order structure in neuroimaging data, including functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), and magnetoencephalography (MEG). Despite the proliferation of proposed measures, the meaning of "higher-order" is often left implicit, and the term is used inconsistently across studies. In this work, we clarify the distinction between higher-order interactions and higher-order dependencies. Higher-order interactions necessarily imply higher-order dependencies, but the converse does not hold: systems can exhibit higher-order dependencies in the absence of higher-order interactions, as in the case of Gaussian variables. We present several equivalent definitions of higher-order interactions for continuous data, illustrate them using simple model systems, and use them to assess the specificity of measures commonly applied in neuroimaging. We show that these measures are not specific to higher-order interactions. Consequently, although existing studies support the presence of higher-order dependencies in neuroimaging data, they do not provide conclusive evidence for the presence of higher-order interactions.

papers.title: Shared Decision Making and Health-Related Quality of Life in Atopic Dermatitis and Chronic Urticaria.
papers.abstract: Shared decision-making (SDM) between patients and healthcare professionals is a patient-centered approach that integrates clinical evidence with patient values and preferences to arrive at healthcare decisions. The major components of shared decision making include seeking the patient's participation and forming a partnership, helping the patient explore and compare treatment options, learning about the patient and their preferences, creating choice awareness, and jointly making and evaluating management decisions. Goals of treatment for chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and atopic dermatitis (AD) are to decrease inflammation in the skin for AD and raised welts/angioedema for CSU, reduce itching and scratching, restore the skin barrier, minimize sleep disturbance, and improve health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Given the growing number of therapeutic options for patients with AD and CSU, shared decision-making has become increasingly important for selecting the best treatment option for each patient and family, in consideration of their unique values, preferences, risk-benefit analysis and outcome priorities, including the impact of treatment on health-related HRQOL. Here, we provide an overview of SDM and HRQoL in patients with chronic spontaneous, chronic inducible urticaria and atopic dermatitis.
papers.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice

papers.title: When emotion meets conflict: Additive but not synergistic effects in neural oscillatory activity.
papers.abstract: Cognitive control allows individuals to regulate their behavior in the face of conflicting or distracting information. Growing evidence suggests that emotional states-particularly self-related emotions-can modulate these control processes. This study explored neural mechanisms underlying amplification of the conflict-adaptation effect (CAE) by self-related emotions, replicating Landman and van Steenbergen (2020). Electroencephalogram (EEG) data were analyzed during two successive trials (Trial N-1 and Trial N) in a prime-probe task. Corrugator muscle activity was also measured as an index of emotional valence. Orthogonal to conflict, word emotion (unpleasant and neutral) and its social context (self- and sender-related) were manipulated. We hypothesized that the emotional facilitation of conflict adaptation by self-related emotional words in Trial N-1 is driven by an affective amplification of conflict-related brain signals. Our behavioral results revealed that emotional words tended to increase CAE, but this effect was threshold-dependent and we failed to replicate the moderation by social context. At the neural level, we replicated earlier results related to conflict and cognitive control; conflict induced early theta synchronization in fronto-central areas and late alpha desynchronization in centro-parietal areas during Trial N-1. Those oscillations showed CAE patterns mirroring the behavioral effect in Trial N. Incongruence increased corrugator activity, indicating that conflict induced unpleasant emotion. Emotion induced neural modulation overlapping with the conflict processing observed in the theta and alpha frequency ranges, suggesting additive but not synergistic effects. Our results reveal neural modulation by conflict and emotional words that might provide input for downstream processes that integrate these signals to drive emotional modulation of behavioral adaptation.
papers.journal: International journal of psychophysiology : official journal of the International Organization of Psychophysiology

papers.title: The role of polysomnography in Parkinson's disease: objective sleep assessment and clinical indications.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders (SDs) are highly prevalent in Parkinson's disease (PD), affecting up to 80% of patients during the disease and significantly contributing to impaired quality of life, cognitive decline, motor worsening, fall risk, and increased caregiver burden. Polysomnography (PSG) remains the gold standard for objective sleep assessment in PD and plays a central role in differential diagnosis and therapeutic planning. This review examines the spectrum of SDs identifiable by PSG, including rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD), obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), periodic limb movements in sleep, and alterations in sleep architecture. Video-polysomnography (v-PSG) is essential for confirming REM sleep without atonia (RWA), which is the electrophysiological hallmark of RBD and a recognized prodromal marker of synucleinopathies. Also, PSG quantifies the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), oxygen desaturation burden, and sleep fragmentation, parameters associated with cognitive impairment and disease progression. While home sleep apnea testing (HSAT, type 3) may be useful for selected cases with high suspicion of OSA, comprehensive in-laboratory (type 1) PSG provides superior diagnostic accuracy, particularly in patients with complex or overlapping sleep disturbances. Integrating objective sleep evaluation into routine PD management is crucial to identify treatable comorbidities, improve prognostic stratification, and optimize motor and non-motor outcomes.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of a family-based graphical tool for longitudinal monitoring of poststroke sequelae.
papers.abstract: Medical information regarding patient health is traditionally managed by healthcare professionals, often leaving patients and families in a passive role during the recovery process. To describe and evaluate a family-based functional graphic tool-the Family Observation of Limits and Learning on Well-being (FOLLOW)-designed for the monthly assessment of post-stroke sequelae by nonprofessionals. The tool is a color-coded visual graphic (red for no improvement, yellow for stability, and green for improvement) designed for intuitive understanding without specialized training. It evaluates seven domains: motor independence, sleep patterns, cognition and language, family quality of life, patient quality of life, fatigue, and emotional state. This study included 51 patients and assessed the usability and proficiency evaluation among three groups: family caregivers, healthcare professionals, and poststroke individuals. Significant differences were observed in the proficiency of completing the tool across the groups. Success rates were 94.1% for family caregivers and 100.0% for healthcare professionals, compared with 69.2% for poststroke individuals (p = 0.008). The graphic proved to be easily interpretable for both caregivers and professionals. The functional graphic is an effective tool when completed by family members or caregivers, though it is less reliable when completed by patients themselves. It provides a practical, longitudinal overview of the patient's home environment and clinical needs, while also serving as a complementary monitoring aid that enables early identification of complications and facilitating prompt intervention.

papers.title: Dynamic Atlas and Functional Regulatory Network of the Whole-Brain Proteome Across 24-Hour Temporal States in Vespertilio sinensis.
papers.abstract: As the only mammals capable of powered flight, bats exhibit extreme metabolic fluctuations adapted to flight and a nocturnal lifestyle, making them unique models for studying diurnal rhythms and energy homeostasis. We performed directDIA-based quantitative proteomics on whole-brain tissues of Vespertilio sinensis across four distinct 24-hour physiological states: Rest, Sleep, Wake, and Activity. Among the 7652 identified proteins, a total of 643 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were screened via pairwise comparisons across timepoints. Time-series clustering further resolved two statistically significant temporal expression modules (Module 3 and Module 9). Combined with functional enrichment of DEPs and phase set enrichment analysis (PSEA) of 574 rhythmic proteins, our multi-layered omics results collectively uncovered stage-specific molecular adaptive patterns. The Active state upregulated oxidative phosphorylation and thermogenesis for high energy demands, the Rest state activated immune clearance and autophagy to eliminate flight-induced metabolic damage, the Sleep state suppressed global transcription, calcium signaling and DNA repair to reduce neural energy consumption, and the Wake state (pre-dusk) pre-activated sulfur biosynthesis, antioxidant defense, and energy metabolic pathways to prepare for upcoming nocturnal activity. Parallel transcriptomic and proteomic rhythmic analysis further identified 19 conserved oscillatory molecules at both molecular layers, revealing partial transcript-protein rhythmic decoupling in the bat brain and refining the diurnal regulatory landscape. As the first systematic atlas of the bat whole-brain proteome across a 24-hour cycle, this study uncovers molecular strategies maintaining brain homeostasis, providing a foundation for understanding diurnal physiological adaptation, flight energy regulation, and circadian output pathways.

papers.title: Intestinal Epithelial Bmal1 Contributes to High-Fat Diet-Induced Hepatic Lipid Dysmetabolism through Microbiota-Associated Bile Acid Remodeling.
papers.abstract: High-fat diet (HFD)-induced hepatic lipid dysmetabolism is closely associated with gut microbiota and bile acid remodeling, but the contribution of intestinal epithelial Bmal1 remains unclear. Here, intestinal epithelial Bmal1 deletion in HFD-fed mice reduced weight gain, improved glucose and lipid homeostasis, and attenuated hepatic steatosis. These changes were accompanied by coordinated regulation of hepatic lipid metabolic pathways, altered bile acid-related signaling along the gut-liver axis, and selective remodeling of the HFD-associated gut microbiota. Targeted analysis further revealed distinct shifts in circulating and fecal bile acid profiles. Fecal microbiota transplantation from HFD-fed Bmal1-deficient donors was associated with similar hepatic metabolic and bile acid-related changes in HFD-fed recipients. Together, these findings support a model in which intestinal epithelial Bmal1 contributes to HFD-induced hepatic lipid dysmetabolism in association with microbiota-associated bile acid remodeling.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Probing the pH- and Voltage-Driven Intramolecular Folding Dynamics of the c-MycC52 Promoter i-Motif at the Single-Molecule Level.
papers.abstract: The human c-Myc proto-oncogene is a transcription factor that regulates protein expression and is controlled by GC-rich regulatory sequences capable of adopting non-canonical DNA secondary structures. Here, we use the α-hemolysin (α-HL) protein nanopore to probe pH- and voltage-dependent effects on the stability of the i-motif formed by the 52-nucleotide cytosine-rich c-Myc promoter (c-MycC52). Under acidic conditions, electrophoretically driven c-MycC52 i-motifs are transiently trapped within the α-HL vestibule, generating pH-dependent electrical current signatures that are volumetrically and kinetically distinct and resolvable at the single-molecule level. The larger molecular volume measured in the acidic pH range, compared with that of linearized DNA at neutral pH, is consistent with the formation of an i-motif. In contrast, the applied transmembrane voltage does not induce detectable changes in the topology of the captured i-motif fragments. Kinetic modeling of current fluctuations within a continuous-time Markov chain framework reveals a subtle coupling between the acidic pH-dependent compaction topology of the captured i-motif and its local interactions with the α-HL vestibule interior and constriction zone. Although molar KCl concentrations (1 and 3 M) yield c-MycC52 i-motif structures of comparably similar volumes at low pH, reduced charge screening at lower ionic strength enhances electrostatic repulsion along the negatively charged DNA backbone, rendering the vestibule-captured folded structure kinetically more stable and more effective at occluding the α-HL constriction. These findings establish α-HL electrophysiology as a sensitive platform for distinguishing subtle differences in i-motif conformational stability, with potential applications in DNA secondary structure dynamics and disease-targeted diagnostic strategies.

papers.title: A3M-CIR: An Attention-Aware Adversarial Masking Based Self-Supervised Chemometric Framework for Robust Infrared Spectral Analysis.
papers.abstract: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy provides rich molecular fingerprint information and is widely used for qualitative and quantitative chemical analysis across biomedical, environmental, and materials science applications. However, its practical utilization is often constrained by instrument-dependent variability, baseline drift, acquisition noise, and limited labeled data. While deep-learning-based chemometric methods have improved performance over traditional preprocessing-driven pipelines, their reliance on supervised learning limits robustness and transferability across heterogeneous measurement conditions. To address these challenges, we introduce A3M-CIR, an attention-aware adversarial masking-based self-supervised chemometric framework for robust infrared spectral analysis. The framework performs large-scale self-supervised pretraining on diverse unlabeled IR spectra to learn transferable representations without explicit calibration or manual annotation. Its core component, the Attention-Aware Adversarial Feature Masking Block (A3FMB), suppresses diagnostically salient absorption regions to generate informative contrastive views that emulate realistic perturbations, while a lightweight Dual-Mixing Attention (DMA) encoder captures both global spectral context and local continuity of one-dimensional vibrational signals. Extensive evaluations under linear-probing and fine-tuning protocols demonstrate consistent improvements over representative self-supervised baselines, and systematic signal-to-noise ratio analyses further validate robustness and transferability under varying noise conditions. By explicitly addressing spectral variability, measurement noise, and limited supervision as intrinsic challenges of infrared spectroscopy, this work establishes A3M-CIR as a practical and extensible foundation for data-driven infrared spectral analysis.

papers.title: Correction to "Short-Term PM2.5 Exposure Impairs Cognitive Function and the DNA Methylation Signatures of Circadian Rhythm Genes".
Single-Particle Microplastics Analysis via Laser-Assisted MicroPyrolysis Flowing Atmospheric-Pressure Afterglow Mass Spectrometry Imaging.
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as ubiquitous contaminants in the environment. Thus, novel MP characterization techniques are in urgent demand to achieve the necessary environmental monitoring, as well as studying the impact of MPs on human health. Herein, laser-assisted micropyrolysis flowing atmospheric pressure afterglow high-resolution mass spectrometry (LAMP FAPA MS) is developed toward direct imaging of single-particle MPs collected on filters. The use of a CO2 laser (10.6 μm) is shown to yield up to >100× higher signal intensity for polyethylene terephthalate fragment ions compared to a diode laser (405 nm) at the same power. Also, a mass spectral analysis algorithm was developed and implemented for fast polymer identification in MPs based on the corresponding fragment ion series separated by the repeating base unit. Furthermore, additive identification is shown for single-particle MPs. Finally, LAMP FAPA MS is demonstrated for quantitative analysis of polymer mass with a detection limit of 0.083 ng for polyethylene microspheres, which corresponds to a spherical particle with a 5.4 μm diameter.

papers.title: Cyclo(Val-Pro), a Potential Plant Immunomodulator, Confers Rice Blast Resistance via Circadian-Clock-Modulated Immune Activation and Metabolic Reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Rice blast, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, is a devastating disease threatening global rice production, with current control strategies facing resistance and environmental risks. Small bioactive peptides have emerged as promising eco-friendly plant immunomodulators with low resistance risk for sustainable crop disease control. Here, we identified cyclic dipeptide cyclo(Val-Pro) as a potential plant immunomodulator with no direct fungicidal activity, which effectively conferred robust rice resistance to M. oryzae via promoting host intrinsic defense responses. Pre-treatment with cyclo(Val-Pro) activated salicylic acid (SA)- and jasmonic acid (JA)-mediated innate immunity, triggered reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and callose deposition, and modulated core circadian clock genes in rice leaves. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis revealed that optimal blast resistance efficacy by cyclo(Val-Pro) pre-treatment at 14:00 was associated with circadian clock regulation and metabolic reprogramming. Specifically, cyclo(Val-Pro) rewired phenylpropanoid and tryptophan metabolism in rice leaves, and tryptamine was validated as a key functional downstream metabolite.
papers.journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

papers.title: Multi-Scale No-Pooling Network for Geographical Origin Identification of Boletus via SERS.
papers.abstract: Frequent poisoning incidents associated with Boletus mushroom highlight the urgent need for rapid trace detection and precise geographical traceability to ensure public safety. However, traditional spectral analysis faces severe bottlenecks due to the strong interference of complex biological matrices and the highly overlapped spectral characteristics among different origins. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a collaborative strategy combining surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) technology and a deep learning framework. Using gold nanorods (Au NRs) as the SERS enhancement substrate, the ultra-sensitive detection of the Boletus toxin protein bolesatine peptide was achieved, and key molecular fingerprint information such as tryptophan (733 cm-1) and tyrosine (634 cm-1) could be effectively detected from complex matrices. Subsequently, a multi-scale no-pooling network (MNNet) was constructed, innovatively adopting a dual-stream parallel architecture, which can simultaneously encode microscopic fingerprint details and macroscopic spectral contour trends. The model directly introduced the "no-pooling" mechanism, discarding the downsampling operation in traditional convolutional networks, thereby strictly preserving the spectral-index-to-wavenumber correspondence of Raman shifts and effectively avoiding the loss of key chemical structure information. Under the current internal evaluation setting, the MNNet-SVM framework achieved an accuracy of 97.69% in classifying Boletus samples from four geographical origins and outperformed the tested one-dimensional comparison frameworks. SHAP interpretation and spectral-window masking further indicated that the classification relied on distributed spectral information rather than exclusively on the dominant bolesatine-associated bands. This study successfully established a promising SERS-assisted multivariate analytical strategy for the detection of toxic components and origin identification in complex public safety systems.

papers.title: DeepSpectrum: A Universal and Accurate Spectral Multimodal Analysis Framework for Lung Cancer Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: In recent years, spectroscopic technology has become a key tool in clinical diagnosis. However, the traditional single-modal spectral analysis method often struggles to capture the full biochemical complexity of heterogeneous biological samples, resulting in limited chemical interpretability and diagnostic sensitivity. To address these challenges, a novel multimodal spectroscopic analysis framework called DeepSpectrum is proposed. It combines the Spectral Mamba and bidirectional gated recurrent unit architectures to enable high-precision lung cancer diagnosis. Specifically, the spectral signals are converted into multichannel image modalities using the continuous wavelet transform (CWT) and Gramian angular difference fields (GADF), thereby constructing rich multimodal data sets. Subsequently, the DeepSpectrum framework is trained, validated, and tested on multimodal spectral data sets, including Raman, Fourier transform infrared, UV-vis absorbance, and fluorescence spectra. It achieved accuracy rates of 98.1%, 98.5%, 92.0%, and 89.2% in lung cancer diagnosis, demonstrating broad applicability across spectral types and complex biological samples. Compared with 11 existing single-modal and multimodal methods, DeepSpectrum showed clear advantages across all evaluation metrics. To further explain the model's decision-making basis, weighted class activation mapping is used to analyze the spectral signals of normal and cancer samples. The model focuses on key regions such as 1127-1375 cm-1 (heme/hemoglobin vibrations) and 1447 cm-1 (lipid metabolism) in Raman spectra, as well as 1000-1140 cm-1 (nucleic acids) in FTIR spectra. These peak values correspond to the evolution process of lung cancer. This not only validates the biochemical interpretability of the DeepSpectrum model but also provides a reliable diagnostic tool for the precise clinical identification of lung cancer.

papers.title: Functional stratification of YWHAZ variants explains distinct neurodevelopmental disorders.
papers.abstract: The application of clinical genomics in personalized medical practice increasingly reveals that variants from single loci can lead to phenotypic heterogeneity. This necessitates functional characterization and classification of serial variants to correlate their associated clinical features and molecular properties. Recently, a few putative pathogenic variants in YWHAZ, encoding the 14-3-3ζ protein, have been implicated in clinically variable isolated and syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotypes, based on a few reported affected individuals, but the molecular basis of this heterogeneity has remained unclear. Here, we assembled a large cohort of individuals harboring de novo YWHAZ variants and categorized their clinical stratification into distinct neurodevelopmental conditions, including a typical presentation of cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome and a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with sleep disorders. By integrating structural analyses, molecular dynamics simulations, in vitro biochemical and cell-based signaling studies, unbiased proteomics analysis, and in vivo phenotypic assays, we define distinct functional classes of pathogenic YWHAZ variants and establish robust genotype-phenotype correlations. We show that disease-associated YWHAZ variants differentially perturb 14-3-3ζ function by variably affecting protein abundance and binding to interacting partners, including the BRAF and RAF1 kinases. Notably, the recurrent p.Ser230Trp (c.689C>G) variant uniquely underlying cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome specifically enhances MAPK signaling, whereas other variants do not significantly impact signal flow through the cascade under the used experimental conditions. Our data establish a mechanistic framework linking allelic variation in YWHAZ to phenotypic heterogeneity.

papers.title: The sleep-wake circuit plays a role in temporal distortions.
papers.abstract: Normally individuals give a fairly accurate subjective estimate of short seconds-to-minutes time interval durations. However, in some circumstances such as a high fever, sudden fear, and old age, temporal distortions can occur so that a conscious individual experiences the passage of subjective time that differs substantially from the actual measured time. Behaviors associated with these temporal distortions and with time perception in general are consistent with the existence of a neural clock circuit in the brain for estimating the passage of short time intervals, but experimental studies to date have generally been limited in demonstrating such a neural circuit. Here we propose that, unexpectedly, actions of the well-known sleep-wake neural circuit are ultimately responsible for many of these known temporal distortions given two basic hypotheses about the underlying electromagnetic nature of the brain. We review this concept, including the theoretical existence of an imaginary-valued pacemaker signal that moves through time along with the brain. We describe the details of this sleep-wake circuit hypothesis, the two main existing theoretical ideas that underlie it, its consistency with currently proposed specific mechanisms of temporal distortions, and how the sleep-wake circuit can serve as a final common route for these specific mechanisms. Importantly, we also show that the sleep-wake circuit hypothesis is readily testable - that it can be falsified using existing experimental methods.
