Flexible SERS sensor with piezoelectric enrichment based on PVDF/AgNWs for cortisol detection in sweat.
papers.abstract: Wearable sensing platforms for non-invasive monitoring of stress biomarkers in sweat are highly desirable for personalized health management. This work presents a flexible surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensor with piezoelectric enrichment based on a PVDF/AgNWs composite membrane for sensitive detection of cortisol. The PVDF fibrous membrane is prepared by electrospinning, which endows it with a high β-phase content and good piezoelectric response. Under mechanical bending, the piezoelectric PVDF membrane generates a non-uniform electric field that polarizes the neutral cortisol molecules, driving them toward the AgNW-decorated SERS hotspots via dielectrophoretic forces, thereby achieving active analyte enrichment without an external power source. In artificial sweat, it shows a wide linear range of 1.0 × 10-9 to 1.0 × 10-5 M and a low detection limit of 1.3 × 10-10 M, along with acceptable uniformity and mechanical robustness. The sensor was further assembled into a wearable patch and preliminarily evaluated using human sweat samples collected during sleep, normal activity, and exercise. Differences in SERS intensity were observed among these states. This flexible SERS sensor shows promise for non-invasive detection of cortisol in sweat and offers a potential strategy for wearable hormone monitoring.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy

papers.title: Mechanically robust and breathable ultrathin nanofiber/hydrogel composite electronic skin for continuous electrophysiological signal acquisition.
papers.abstract: Flexible bioelectronic devices are crucial for continuous, non-invasive health monitoring, yet achieving ultrathin structures while maintaining mechanical stability and signal fidelity remains challenging. Herein, an ultrathin fiber-reinforced hydrogel electronic skin (CFPIG) with a thickness of ~5.3 μm is developed by embedding polyurethane (PU) nanofibers into a hydrogel matrix combined with a freeze-thaw/UV dual-crosslinking strategy. This synergistic design significantly enhances crystallinity and mechanical performance, achieving a tear strength of 1.3 kJ·m-2, toughness of ~621 kJ·m-3, and stable performance after 300 stretching cycles at 60% strain. Incorporation of the ionic liquid BMIM OTf further constructs an efficient ion-conduction network, improving electrochemical performance. Benefiting from the synergistic effect of the ultrathin structure and porous fiber network, CFPIG exhibits excellent skin conformability, stable interfacial adhesion energy (~158 μJ·cm-2), and high water vapor permeability (~1690 g·m-2·day-1), enabling long-term comfortable skin attachment. CFPIG enables high-fidelity acquisition of multimodal electrophysiological signals, including EMG, ECG, and EEG, with low noise and drift under dynamic conditions. Combined with convolutional neural network analysis, the system achieves over 95% accuracy in hand gesture recognition, demonstrating strong potential for wearable health monitoring and intelligent human-machine interaction systems.
papers.journal: Journal of colloid and interface science

papers.title: Cloud based solid state NMR automated processing (SNAP): A digital solution to enable efficient and robust data analysis.
papers.abstract: Solid state NMR (ssNMR) enables molecular level structural interrogation across drug discovery and development, and specifically, the stability assessment of chemical and biological therapeutics. However, routine application in pharmaceutical settings is constrained by inherently low sensitivity, complex data analysis, and fragmented workflows that rely on multiple proprietary software packages, limiting accessibility, throughput, and reproducibility. Herein, we developed Solid-state NMR Automated Processing (SNAP), a cloud-based software platform with a web interface designed to streamline ssNMR data handling. SNAP imports raw NMR free induction decay (FID) signals, automates preprocessing, performs spectral fitting, and enables graphical spectral analysis. The platform consolidates discrete file transformation steps into a single, automated workflow and supports standardized export to reporting documentation. We demonstrated across representative ssNMR datasets that SNAP reduced manual steps, simplified multistage processing, and improved the consistency of spectral analysis and reporting relative to conventional approaches that require multiple software tools. The consolidated workflow increased efficiency and supported reproducible quantification. By integrating acquisition-to-reporting tasks into a single, automated pipeline, SNAP enhances throughput, robustness, and confidence in ssNMR data processing and quantification. This digital solution is designed to improve the accessibility and efficiency of ssNMR in pharmaceutical development.
papers.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis

papers.title: Clinical, immunological and metabolic features and gut-brain axis markers in children with autism spectrum disorder and TORCH-associated central nervous system involvement.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) have heterogeneous etiologies, with TORCH infections potentially contributing to neurodevelopmental disruption through central nervous system injury and gut-brain axis dysfunction. A prospective comparative study enrolled 280 children aged 3-10 years with ASD: 112 with TORCH-associated central nervous system (CNS) involvement (main group) and 168 with idiopathic ASD (comparison group), alongside 25 healthy controls. Assessments included clinical/neurological features, autism severity, gastrointestinal symptoms, pro-inflammatory cytokines, metabolic markers, neuron-specific enolase (NSE), fecal zonulin, and brain MRI. TORCH pathogens were detected by PCR from saliva samples. TORCH-associated ASD exhibited a more severe phenotype with greater frequencies of delayed speech, cognitive impairment, sleep disturbance, hyperactivity, emotional-behavioral dysregulation, epileptiform manifestations, and gastrointestinal symptoms. Severe ASD was significantly more common in the TORCH group. Laboratory analyses revealed significantly elevated interleukin-1β, interleukin-8, tumor necrosis factor alpha, homocysteine, ammonia, uric acid, NSE, and fecal zonulin, with reduced folate. Fecal zonulin was positively correlated with inflammatory markers and neuron-specific enolase. MRI more frequently demonstrated periventricular gliosis, ventriculomegaly, subependymal abnormalities, and diffuse residual organic changes. In this cohort, ASD with clinical evidence of TORCH-associated CNS involvement was associated with greater clinical severity and higher serum inflammatory, metabolic, neuronal-injury, fecal-zonulin, and structural MRI measures than ASD without such evidence. The cross-sectional design and limitations of salivary PCR preclude causal attribution to TORCH infection.

papers.title: Neural representations expand with aging but collapse in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Neural activity continuously changes over time, yet how these changes relate to cognitive states and disease remains unclear. We modeled EEG activity as distributions of short-term activity patterns and quantified distributional changes using Wasserstein distance. Intrinsic dimensionality was estimated to characterize representational complexity and its association with these changes. Across multi-task, lifespan, and clinical EEG datasets, higher intrinsic dimensionality was consistently associated with greater distributional changes. Healthy aging showed increased dimensionality and modestly increased displacement, whereas mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease showed reduced dimensionality and displacement, indicating distinct alterations in representational geometry. Cognitive aging and impairment are associated with distinct alterations in the geometry of neural representations. A geometric perspective on neural representations provides a complementary approach for characterizing cognitive states and brain dynamics across aging and disease.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Age-specific associations of estrone sulfate, DHEAS, and anti-Müllerian hormone with depressive symptom dimensions in men.
papers.abstract: Sex hormones influence brain circuits that regulate mood, but previous studies in men have focused on few hormones and treated depression as a single condition. In a nationally representative sample of men, we systematically examine 12 serum sex hormones across the adult lifespan in relation to dimensional depressive symptoms. We analyzed cross-sectional data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2017-2023). Serum sex hormones were measured, and depressive symptoms were assessed by PHQ-9, with a score ≥5 indicating mild or greater symptoms. Survey-weighted regression models examined associations between hormones and depressive symptoms, total scores, somatic/non-somatic subscales, and nine individual symptoms. Among 5668 men (mean age 51.1 years), 1344 (23.7%) had depressive symptoms. Higher anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH, OR=0.86), dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS, OR=0.83), and estrone sulfate (ES1, OR=0.87) were associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms; higher luteinizing hormone (LH, OR=1.11) with increased odds. Age-stratified analyses showed ES1 was inversely associated with depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older men, DHEAS only in older men, and AMH in younger and middle-aged men. Dimensionally, ES1, AMH, and testosterone were associated with lower somatic symptom scores (β=-0.12, -0.16, and -0.17), while AMH was also associated with lower non-somatic scores (β=-0.23). AMH was inversely associated with concentration difficulties; FSH and LH with sleep disturbance. Sex hormones show distinct, age and symptom-dimension-specific associations with male depression, challenging unitary diagnostic approaches. These findings support hormone-informed subtyping of male depression and suggest clinical assessment should consider both age and symptom presentation.

papers.title: Diagnostic and mechanistic insights from molecular profiling of explanted stereo-EEG depth electrodes.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy surgery involving deep brain stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) offers a unique window into the biology of epilepsy in living humans. Explanted SEEG electrodes retain nucleic acids, enabling identification of somatic variants underlying treatment-resistant epilepsies. Recent studies show SEEG depth electrodes also preserve trace material sufficient for high-quality, region-specific transcriptomic and epigenetic profiling at near-contact resolution, distinguishing seizure onset, propagation and non-involved zones within individuals. We review these advances, focusing on methodologies, how molecular landscapes reflect cellular composition and activity states, and their integration with neurophysiology and clinical data. SEEG-derived molecular profiling captures dynamic brain states with unprecedented spatial and functional resolution, with applications in molecular diagnosis, surgical decision-making and uncovering disease mechanisms to inform future interventions and improve epilepsy management outcomes.

papers.title: Upadacitinib for the Management of Atopic Dermatitis in Patients Aged ≥60 Years: A Long-Term Multicenter Real-World Study.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) in the elderly is increasing worldwide and presents therapeutic challenges due to age-related comorbidities that often contraindicate systemic therapies. Although oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors show efficacy in moderate-to-severe AD, older adult patients are underrepresented in clinical trials, and regulators recommend caution in this population. We conducted a multicenter, retrospective, observational study at 15 Italian university hospitals, including patients with moderate-to-severe AD aged ≥60 years treated with upadacitinib 15 or 30 mg once daily, to evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of this selective JAK1 inhibitor at weeks 16, 32, 52, and 104. Seventy-two patients were included (mean age 65.9 ± 6.4 years); 48/72 (66.7%) of patients showed a classical flexural phenotype; 34/72 (47.2%) presented with head-and-neck involvement. Upadacitinib led to marked and sustained improvement in both clinician-and-patient-reported outcomes, with mean Eczema Area and Severity Index decreasing from 23.9 ± 9.2 at baseline to 1.5 ± 3.0 at week 52 and 0.9 ± 2.5 at week 104. Mean itch-Numeric Rating Scales (NRS) decreased from 8.2 ± 2.0 at baseline to 1.0 ± 1.9 at week 52 and 1.0 ± 2.4 at week 104, with concomitant amelioration in sleep-NRS (6.5 ± 3.1 to 0.5 ± 1.6 and 0.3 ± 1.3) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (16.8 ± 6.9 to 1.6 ± 4.2 and 1.0 ± 3.2). Adverse events occurred in 37/72 (51,4%) patients and included dyslipidemia in 22/72 (30.6%) patients, creatine phosphokinase elevation in 15/72 (20.8%), and blood count abnormalities in 13/72 (18.1%); they were mostly mild and manageable. Overall, 16/72 patients (22.2%) discontinued treatment, including 11/72 (15.3%) due to AEs. In our multicenter real-world cohort of patients aged ≥60 years, upadacitinib demonstrated rapid, sustained efficacy and an overall favorable safety profile through 104 weeks, supporting its long-term use in clinical practice with appropriate monitoring.

papers.title: Secukinumab for Refractory Psoriasiform Cutaneous Manifestations in CTSC-Syndromic Epidermal Differentiation Disorder: A Pediatric Case Report.
papers.abstract: CTSC-syndromic epidermal differentiation disorder is a rare autosomal recessive genodermatosis caused by loss-of-function mutations in the cathepsin C gene. It is characterized by palmoplantar keratoderma and early-onset periodontal destruction, and no standardized disease-specific therapy has been established. We report a 3-year-old boy with disease onset in infancy, presenting with palmoplantar and generalized erythematous scaly lesions, severe pruritus, sleep disturbance, and nail roughness. Whole-exome sequencing followed by Sanger sequencing identified compound heterozygous variants in the cathepsin C gene: c.774C>G inherited from his father and c.328G>T inherited from his mother. Treatment with cyclosporine combined with systemic retinoids failed to prevent disease progression. After pretreatment evaluation and written informed consent from his guardian, secukinumab was administered subcutaneously at a dose of 75 mg at weeks 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, followed by once every 4 weeks thereafter. After 12 weeks of treatment, the patient showed marked improvement in clinical manifestations, quality-of-life scores, and disease severity scores, with no infectious complications during treatment at our institution. After secukinumab was continued locally, an infection involving the right foot and ankle led to treatment discontinuation, and a pulmonary infection was reported during later follow-up.

papers.title: Aperiodic EEG activity is a domain-specific marker of attentional aging in neurotypical adults.
papers.abstract: Aperiodic neural activity has been reliably shown to be reduced among older adults, and these reductions are associated with age-related cognitive decline. These results suggest that aperiodic activity, as measured by the spectral exponent, might be a viable electrophysiological biomarker for cognitive aging. However, this has not been tested longitudinally, within participants, during normal aging. Here, we used a longitudinal cohort of either sex to test whether changes in aperiodic activity between two sessions, approximately 5 years apart, track behavioral change across two domains: sustained attention (Psychomotor Vigilance Test) and executive function (modified Simon task). We found that aperiodic activity declined within individuals after the interval, independent of age at baseline. This within-person change tracked concurrent changes in reaction times during sustained attention but was not associated with changes in any Simon task measure. Within a resampling framework, the aperiodic-PVT association was stable across cohort resamples and independently fitted partitions, though it was not confirmed in a small, frozen held-out set. These findings suggest the longitudinal decline in aperiodic activity tracks attentional processing speed rather than executive function, supporting its potential as a domain-specific biomarker of attentional aging in neurotypical populations.Significance Statement Aperiodic (non-oscillatory) neural activity, indexed by the aperiodic exponent, is known to decline in older adults, but whether this happens within individuals over just a few years, and in step with cognitive change, remains unclear. Here we leveraged scalp EEG and cognitive-behavioral data from 276 neurotypical adults, tested twice approximately five years apart, and found that the aperiodic exponent declines within individuals over this interval, independent of age at baseline. This decline tracked concurrent slowing on a sustained attention task, but not change on an executive function task, and only in EEG recorded before, not after, cognitive testing. Based on this dissociation, we propose that aperiodic exponent decline indexes attentional processing speed rather than general cognitive decline in neurotypical aging.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience

papers.title: Probing the neural geometry of conscious object perception in time.
papers.abstract: Conscious object recognition is a critical brain function, key to making sense of the plethora of visual inputs and guiding adaptive behavior. Yet, the sequence of neural processing underlying conscious object recognition remains unclear. Existing proposals alternatively suggest that conscious object recognition proceeds in a "coarse-to-fine" sequence or a "fine-to-coarse" sequence. Here, we recorded high-density EEG while participants of both sexes performed a threshold-level object recognition task under different viewing conditions. Both superordinate and basic-level category information emerged early in neural activity, followed by a late superordinate category representation in an abstract format that is disentangled from low-level object features. Strikingly, in the early period, while basic-level category information positively correlated with perceptual awareness, superordinate category information negatively predicted perceptual awareness. By contrast, both superordinate and basic-level category information positively correlated with objective categorization accuracy in the early period. In the late period, both levels of category information positively correlated with awareness. These results suggest that neural processing underlying conscious object perception proceeds from the basic to the superordinate category level.Significance statement Despite significant interests, the sequence of neural processing underlying conscious perception remains unclear. Here, we investigated the unfolding of neural events in time that support perceptual awareness of visual objects. Using a threshold-level object perception task involving three image conditions (normal, low-pass filtered, masked) and high-density EEG, we reveal that basic and superordinate category information both emerge early in the neural activity (at ∼100 ms), but only the basic-level category representation positively contributes to awareness. By contrast, the early superordinate category representation negatively correlates with perceptual awareness. At ∼300 ms, an abstract superordinate category representation emerges, which also positively correlates with perceptual awareness. Therefore, category-level neural processing underlying conscious object perception proceeds from the basic to the superordinate level.

papers.title: Identification of lipoxygenase inhibitors from litchi shell extract and their potential mechanism in delaying lipid oxidation and off-flavor formation in sunflower seeds.
papers.abstract: Lipoxygenase (LOX) is considered a key target associated with lipid oxidation and quality deterioration of oil-seeds. In this study, high-affinity LOX inhibitors were screened from four plant extracts by UPLC-QTOF-MS, and their possible mechanism in delaying lipid oxidation and off-flavor formation of sunflower seeds was elucidated. Partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLSDA) of LOX activity, electronic nose sensor response components, and oxidation indicator levels data showed that LOX activity was positively correlated with both lipid oxidation and off-flavor formation in sunflower seeds stored at 40 °C for 56 days. Three high-affinity LOX inhibitors, including epicatechin (EC, IC50 = 1.22 ± 0.07 mg/mL), epicatechin gallate (ECG, IC50 = 1.00 ± 0.03 mg/mL) and 6-gingerol (IC50 = 2.86 ± 0.11 mg/mL), were identified from litchi shell extract (LSE), which exhibited the strongest LOX inhibitory activity among 4 plant extracts. EC acted as a competitive inhibitor, whereas ECG and 6-gingerol functioned as mixed inhibitors. The results of multi-spectral analysis, AFM characterization and molecular docking confirmed each other, indicating that hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions of inhibitors with residues of LOX drove the formation of inhibitor-LOX complexes, thereby inducing the changes of enzyme conformation and microenvironment, thus inhibiting the LOX activity, as well as the lipid oxidation and off-flavor of sunflower seeds. These findings propose a novel strategy for delaying lipid oxidation and off-flavor formation via targeted inhibition of LOX activity of oil-seeds and provide a theoretical basis for the application of LSE as a natural antioxidant in the preservation of lipid-rich food.

papers.title: Comparative study of the flavor profile of raw and stir-fried Ziziphi Spinosae Semen.
papers.abstract: Ziziphi Spinosae Semen (ZSS) undergoes marked flavor changes during traditional stir-frying, but its time-dependent flavor evolution and associated neural responses remain unclear. Raw ZSS (F0) and samples stir-fried for 5-30 min (F5-F30) were evaluated using electronic nose, electronic tongue, HS-SPME-GC-MS, GC-IMS and electroencephalography (EEG). Stir-frying reduced bitterness and astringency while enhancing sweetness, umami and richness. The volatile profile shifted from aldehyde- and ketone-associated raw, fatty and oxidized notes toward alcohol-, ester-, furan- and heterocyclic-compound-associated fruity, sweet, roasted and nutty characteristics. HS-SPME-GC-MS showed the highest total internal-standard-equivalent volatile level in F30, whereas GC-IMS revealed stronger characteristic signals in F20-F25 and substantial volatile redistribution in F30. EEG responses increased with stir-frying duration and were strongest in F30, indicating greater neural salience rather than superior flavor quality. Integrated analysis tentatively identified F20-F25 as a balanced processing window for flavor development. These findings provide a multidimensional basis for optimizing the stir-frying quality of ZSS.

papers.title: Multidimensional discrimination of Niulanshan light-flavor baijiu across price categories via integrated volatilome profiling, sensory analysis, and neurophysiological responses.
papers.abstract: Niulanshan light-flavor Baijiu (NLFB) exhibits pronounced price stratification. However, objective criteria for quality grading remain insufficient. This study established a multidimensional framework integrating flavor chemistry and consumer neuroscience to elucidate the molecular and neurophysiological basis of Baijiu quality differentiation. Six NLFB samples spanning three price tiers were evaluated using descriptive sensory analysis, comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC × GC-MS), targeted quantitative analysis, and electroencephalography (EEG). Principal component analysis revealed clear spatial clustering corresponding to distinct quality tiers. Using GC × GC-MS identified 137 volatile compounds, indicating substantial variation in chemical complexity among different NLFBs. Further quantitative analysis identified 29 key marker compounds associated with quality differentiation. Premium-tier samples were characterized by higher concentrations of esters (e.g., ethyl acetate), contributing to a more refined Chen-aroma profile and eliciting increased alpha wave (8-13 Hz) synchronization, indicative of positive hedonic responses. In contrast, economy-tier samples contained elevated levels of higher alcohols (e.g., propanol). Correlation network analysis revealed that these higher alcohols exerted a masking effect on characteristic Zao-aroma compounds, leading to sensory imbalance and increased beta wave (13-30 Hz) activity, indicative of neural irritation. Together, these findings demonstrate that price differentiation in Baijiu is underpinned by distinct chemical matrices and corresponding spatiotemporal EEG dynamics. This neuro-sensory framework provides biologically grounded evidence for objective quality evaluation and grading of NLFB.

papers.title: Influence of different cell wall disruption methods on flavor quality of yeast extract: mechanistic insights through peptidomics and molecular docking.
papers.abstract: Yeast extract (YE) is a widely used natural flavor enhancer whose taste and aroma quality govern its industrial value. However, how the cell wall disruption method, the first and decisive step of YE production, shapes flavor at the molecular level remains unclear, leaving method selection largely empirical. In this study, five representative disruption methods, autolysis (AY), ethyl acetate chemical disruption (EA), high-pressure homogenization (HPH), low-temperature colloid milling (LCM), and glucanase enzymatic hydrolysis (GE), were systematically compared using sensory evaluation, electronic nose and tongue, free amino acid and nucleotide profiling, solvent-assisted flavor evaporation coupled with gas chromatography-olfactometry-mass spectrometry (SAFE-GC-O-MS), electroencephalography (EEG), liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) peptidomics, and molecular docking. Results showed that GE produced the highest umami amino acid content (113.01 mg/g DW, p < 0.05) and the lowest bitterness, whereas EA yielded the highest bitter amino acid proportion; SAFE-GC-O-MS identified 117 volatile compounds, of which 67 (odor activity value ≥1) drove inter-group differentiation, and peptidomics revealed 1785 differential peptides, with GE generating more glutamate/aspartate-rich umami-associated peptides. In addition, molecular docking demonstrated that GE-derived acidic peptides bound the umami receptor T1R1/T1R3 most strongly (ΔG down to -9.18 kcal/mol), whereas EA-derived hydrophobic peptides preferentially engaged the bitter receptors TAS2R13/TAS2R14; synthesized-peptide validation corroborated these predictions (r = 0.93). Therefore, entropy-weighted TOPSIS confirmed the ranking GE > LCM > HPH > EA > AY, and this study establishes a "disruption method to peptide profile to receptor selectivity to flavor quality" framework guiding the industrial production of high-quality YE.

papers.title: Electrode-Modiolar Distance as a Determinant of Cochlear Implant Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: To quantify the relationship between electrode-modiolar distance (EMD) and cochlear implant (CI) performance across speech/perceptual, electrophysiological and programming outcomes and to characterize the dose-response effect of EMD. A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane CENTRAL was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Human studies reporting CT- or CBCT-derived EMD and CI outcomes were included. Effect sizes were transformed to odds ratios (ORs) and pooled using random-effects models. Subgroup, sensitivity and dose-response analyses were performed. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. Twenty-one studies comprising approximately 1181 implanted ears were included. Reduced EMD was associated with significantly higher odds of favourable CI outcomes (pooled OR = 2.16, 95% CI: 1.89-2.45; p < 0.001; I2 = 0%). Consistent effects were observed for speech/perceptual outcomes (OR = 2.23), electrophysiological measures (OR = 2.80 after sensitivity adjustment) and programming parameters (OR = 1.72). Dose-response modelling demonstrated a monotonic gradient, with each 1 mm increase in EMD associated with a 20%-30% reduction in the odds of favourable outcomes (OR per mm ≈0.72; p < 0.001). No significant publication bias was detected (Egger's p = 0.056). Electrode-modiolar proximity is a strong and consistent determinant of CI performance with a clear dose-response relationship, supporting its role as a clinically actionable imaging biomarker for optimizing electrode selection, surgical strategy and individualized programming. PROSPERO: CRD420261380236.
papers.journal: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery

papers.title: Association between maternal traumatic stress related to Great East Japan Earthquake and behavioral problems in offspring.
papers.abstract: : Women who experienced the Great East Japan Earthquake (GEJE) and subsequently became pregnant may have children who are more likely to exhibit emotional and behavioral problems. However, few longitudinal studies have investigated the developmental outcomes among children born to mothers who experienced natural disasters before pregnancy and continued to experience stress symptoms thereafter. : This study aimed to examine the association between maternal traumatic stress related to the GEJE and behavioral problems in their children. : A total of 21,656 mother-child pairs were included in the analysis; 52.0% of the offspring were male. Maternal traumatic stress symptoms related to the GEJE were assessed using items evaluating recollection, emotional distress, somatic reactions, and avoidance behaviors (Cronbach α=0.681). Child behavioral outcomes at 2 and 3 years of age were assessed using the Child Behavior Checklist for Ages 1½-5 (CBCL/1½-5). Missing data were addressed by multiple imputation, and a multivariable logistic regression was performed with adjustment for maternal psychological distress, social isolation, sleep problems, parity, breastfeeding, disaster-related exposure, parental history of mental illness, and socioeconomic characteristics. Covariate selection was guided by a directed acyclic graph. : Compared with mothers who reported no traumatic stress symptoms, those reporting one or 2 symptoms had a higher odds of their children exhibiting internalizing (odds ratio [OR], 1.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-1.69), externalizing (OR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.07-1.55) and total problems (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.11-1.72) at age 2 and internalizing (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.13-1.69), externalizing (OR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.01-1.45) and total problems (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.10-1.71) at age 3. Mothers reporting 3 or 4 symptoms showed stronger associations, a pattern consistent with a dose-response relationship supported by a formal test for trends for most outcomes. These findings were consistent with those of sensitivity analyses using continuous CBCL scores. : These findings suggest that maternal mental health support beyond pregnancy may be important for women of reproductive age in disaster-affected areas and could help inform preventive strategies addressing the intergenerational effects of trauma following largescale disasters such as the GEJE.

papers.title: Nocturnal road traffic noise and Sleep during Mid-Adulthood in Urban Settings: Examining Sex and Socioeconomic Differences within the DAS-EP Project.
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for physical and mental health but tends to deteriorate from mid adulthood, particularly among women. Nocturnal road traffic noise is a major environmental stressor that can disrupt sleep. This study aimed to examine the association between nocturnal road traffic noise and sleep health during mid-adulthood and explore potential sex-based differences. We conducted a cross sectional analysis using data from population health surveys (2021-2023) including 1,898 adults aged 40-60 living in urban areas of the Basque Autonomous Community, the Valencian Community, and Barcelona. Nocturnal road traffic noise was assessed using Lnight indicator, defined as the long-term average noise level during the night-time period (23:00-07:00), and estimated using official noise maps. Sleep health was assessed through self-reported measures of sleep duration, overall sleep satisfaction, and sleep quality using the SATED scale, a multidimensional measure of sleep health (Satisfaction, Alertness, Timing, Efficiency, and Duration). A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) was used to identify covariate adjustment sets and associations were estimated using linear models accounting for the complex survey design. Women generally reported poorer sleep health than men, with lower sleep satisfaction and poorer sleep quality, and sleep quality increased with area-level household income. Noise exposure increased with income at lower levels, while different patterns were observed across regions after €50,000. The association between noise exposure and sleep health varied across regions and sleep health dimensions. In Barcelona, higher noise exposure was associated with greater sleep satisfaction, but this association was not significant in pooled meta analyses. In contrast, higher noise exposure was associated with poorer sleep quality in the Basque Country, with the pooled meta-analysis showing a similar overall pattern. These findings highlight the context-dependent nature of noise-sleep relationships and support the need for targeted public health strategies.

papers.title: Evaluation of novel water soluble compositions of propofol for intravenous anesthesia.
papers.abstract: Solubilizing propofol without lipid-associated risks-hyperlipidemia, microbial growth, and severe injection pain-remains a major formulation challenge spanning over four decades. Traditional lipid emulsions persist largely due to the difficulty of achieving high-capacity aqueous solubilization without compromising safety or stability. This study evaluates a fat-free, preservative-free aqueous 1% propofol formulation enabled by a novel PEG-carbohydrate-lipid conjugate, 3,3-oleoyl-monomethoxy-polyethyleneglycol (n = 12 mean) ether-propanediaminolactobionate ("DOPS-F02"), highlighting its efficiency as an advanced solubilizing excipient for intravenous delivery. Solubilization capacity was profiled alongside a 24-month GLP stability trial of 1% propofol with 2.3% DOPS-F02 in 5% dextrose (Type I glass vials). A fixed-dose combination with 0.11% lidocaine HCl was evaluated without increasing excipient concentration. Pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and nociceptive profiles (rat paw-flick/paw-lick model) were compared against commercial control (Fresofol). DOPS-F02 demonstrated exceptional solubilization efficiency, driving propofol aqueous solubility up to 80 mg/mL at a low 1:2.2 w/w drug-to-solubilizer ratio in 5% dextrose or saline. Autoclaving induced a reversible cloud-point phase transition, returning to a clear, isotropic state upon cooling. Over 24 months, potency remained within ±3% with total impurities below 0.3%. In vivo, DOPS-F02 achieved therapeutic equivalence to Fresofol (loss of righting reflex; sleep duration 7.73-7.83 min). Unlike typical non-lipid formulations that exacerbate injection pain, DOPS-F02 allowed seamless co-formulation with lidocaine without phase separation, mitigating pain to near-baseline levels. As a novel solubilization platform, DOPS-F02 resolves a multi-decade formulation hurdle, delivering a clear, lipid-free propofol system requiring only a 1:2.2 drug-to-solubilizer ratio that eliminates emulsion liabilities and injection pain.

papers.title: Beyond LDL-C: A Case-Based Review of Complex Dyslipidemia.
papers.abstract: Dyslipidemia is clinically heterogeneous, and LDL-C alone may not fully capture atherogenic particle burden, metabolic risk, treatment response, or inherited disease. This case-based review presents three dyslipidemia phenotypes that illustrate common diagnostic and management challenges. The first case describes diet-sensitive LDL particle and lipoprotein insulin resistance changes despite LDL-C values near conventional targets in a patient with subclinical coronary atherosclerosis. The second highlights persistent low HDL-C and HDL particle number despite substantial LDL-C reduction with non-statin and incretin-era therapies in the setting of obesity and strong family history. The third demonstrates genetically confirmed familial hypercholesterolemia due to a pathogenic LDLR variant despite absent classic physical stigmata. Together, these cases support a phenotype-driven approach that integrates LDL-C, ApoB or LDL particle number, diet response, metabolic context, imaging, medication tolerance, and selective genetic testing to individualize dyslipidemia risk assessment and treatment.
papers.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences

papers.title: N-Glycosylation in the Receptor Binding Domain serves as aggregation gatekeeper of the SARS CoV2 Spike glycoprotein folding.
papers.abstract: The SARS CoV2 Spike is a multi-domain surface glycoprotein that binds human ACE2 via its receptor binding domain (RBD-CoV2) initiating the viral infection. Several aggregation prone regions are predicted in the Spike-CoV2 sequence. Here, we describe the intrinsic aggregation feature and characterization of RBD-CoV2 aggregates of the Wuhan variant in the context of its folding. In agreement with its predicted aggregation-prone nature, recombinant RBD-CoV2 in E. coli exclusively forms inclusion bodies that binds Thioflavin S dye. In vitro refolding of pure denatured RBD-CoV2 results in extensive aggregation yielding very low amounts of soluble functional protein. The RBD-CoV2 in vitro aggregates contain β-sheet structure as revealed by the Raman spectral analysis, bind amyloid-specific AmyTracker 630 and ProteoStat dyes, and have clustered sphere-like morphology. Similarly, the non-glycosylated RBD-CoV2 missing the N-glycan on Asn331 and Asn343, an equivalent to EcRBD, is not secreted, but retained in the endoplasmic reticulum of HEK293T cells. The ProteoStat dye binding indicates intracellular accumulation of the N-glycan RBD variants as amyloids in live cells. Furthermore, selective removal of both RBD N-glycans results in severe secretion defect of the Spike ectodomain, and markedly reduced syncytia formation in cells expressing glycan variants of membrane-bound Spike. Our study thus conclusively demonstrates that the essential role of RBD N-glycans is to prevent misfolding and aggregation of RBD-CoV2 and Spike-CoV2. The presence of N-glycan at either one of the two Asn in RBD significantly reduces misfolding of the full length Spike-CoV2, and the absence of both glycans results in RBD-CoV2 to form amyloids.

papers.title: Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
papers.abstract: Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation. To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms. BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device. Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048). In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

papers.title: Effects of cannabidiol (CBD) oral solution in patients undergoing bilateral total knee arthroplasty: a randomized, controlled, parallel, triple blind, pilot study.
papers.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) is a non-intoxicating phytocannabinoid with limited clinical evidence of its analgesic and opioid sparing effects. In the United States, the oral cannabidiol solution, Epidiolex®, is FDA-approved for intractable seizures. We conducted an off-label pilot randomized trial to evaluate its perioperative effects in patients undergoing bilateral total knee arthroplasty (BTKA). After IRB-approval and trial registration (NCT04749628), 36 patients were randomized to receive four perioperative doses of placebo (n=12), 400mg (n=12) or 800mg (n=12) oral CBD with standardized anesthesia and multimodal analgesia. The primary outcome was cumulative 72-hour opioid consumption (MME). Secondary outcomes included pain scores, adjunct analgesic use, inflammatory markers (IL-6), sleep, mood (HADS), safety, and pharmacokinetics. Dunnett's test showed no significant differences in 72-hour opioid consumption versus placebo (400mg: 144 vs 209 MME, p=0.10; 800mg: 203.2 vs 209 MME, p=0.98), although post hoc testing demonstrated lower opioid use with 400mg CBD compared with placebo (p=0.04). The 400mg group also had lower pain scores and fewer rescue analgesic requirements, but greater NSAID use. The 800mg group showed no opioid-sparing effect and had greater adverse event burden. CBD groups reported improved subjective sleep domains, while anxiety and depression scores were higher, particularly at 800mg. IL-6 levels were higher in CBD groups. Pharmacokinetic analyses confirmed measurable, dose-dependent exposure with substantial interindividual variability. These pilot data suggest a potential therapeutic signal at moderate dosing but not at higher doses. Larger trials are needed to confirm efficacy and define optimal dosing. PERSPECTIVE: Among BTKA patients, 400mg cannabidiol reduced opioid use and pain while remaining tolerable, whereas higher dosing increased side effects, supporting further evaluation of CBD analgesia.

papers.title: The Effect of Pet Companionship on Clinical Symptoms in Migraine.
papers.abstract: Migraine is a disabling neurological disorder aggravated by anxiety, sleep disturbance, and chronic stress. Prospective evidence linking pet‑keeping to migraine prognosis is scarce. This study evaluated longitudinal associations of pet ownership with migraine symptoms, comorbidities, and medication use, as well as clinical changes after initiating or stopping pet ownership. This multicenter prospective cohort study enrolled 3017 International Classification of Headache Disorders‑3 (ICHD‑3)‑defined migraine patients with 2‑year standardized follow‑up. Participants were categorized bydynamic pet‑keeping status. Longitudinal outcomes included migraine severity, attack frequency, anxiety, sleep quality, quality of life, and medication utilization; analyses adjusted for baseline imbalances and missing data. Continuous pet ownership was associated with lower migraine attack frequency, reduced pain severity, decreased medication utilization, alleviated anxiety and sleep disturbances, and improved migraine-specific quality of life over 2-year follow-up (all P<0.001). Dog ownership correlated with more favorable clinical profiles versus cat or other pet ownership (P<0.05). New pet acquisition was associated with significant within-subject improvements in clinical outcomes, whereas discontinuation of pet keeping correlated with the reversal of most clinical benefits. Greater total daily human-pet interaction time exhibited graded associative correlations with clinical improvement magnitude. Stable pet companionship, particularly dog ownership, is favorably associated with improved migraine-related symptoms, comorbid psychological and sleep disturbances, and reduced medication demand. Discontinuation of pet ownership correlates with the attenuation of these observational outcomes. Pet companionship may serve as a feasible non-pharmacological adjuvant consideration for comprehensive migraine management.

papers.title: Thermal expansion of anhydrous chitosan crystal.
papers.abstract: Chitosan is a renewable polysaccharide derived from chitin. However, its structure-property relationships remain poorly understood. Specifically, the thermal expansion of anhydrous chitosan crystals has not yet been fully elucidated. In this study, thermal expansion of highly crystalline anhydrous chitosan was investigated using X-ray diffraction and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. X-ray diffraction measurements from 303 to 523 K revealed linear, anisotropic thermal expansion in the orthorhombic lattice, with coefficients of αa = 1.79 × 10-5, αb = 7.16 × 10-5, and αc = 1.06 × 10-5 K-1, and a volumetric coefficient of β = 10.21 × 10-5 K-1. MD simulations reproduced the same order of anisotropy (αb > αa > αc) and showed good quantitative agreement with the experimental volumetric expansion. Further analysis revealed that the observed anisotropy is closely associated with anisotropic phonon-like lattice vibrations: power spectral analysis of chain center-of-mass motions showed pronounced softening of the a-axis mode alongside disappearance of the b-axis mode with increasing temperature, even as the hydrogen-bonding network and overall molecular conformation remained essentially unchanged. These directional differences in vibrational dynamics, together with the directionally distinct nature of intermolecular hydrogen-bonding interactions along each crystallographic axis, are considered to underlie the observed thermal expansion anisotropy, which was thereby elucidated through the combined use of experimental and computational approaches.

papers.title: Attention Load Modulates Functional Brain Connectivity Reorganization in Children with High Autistic Traits: Evidence from Phase and Amplitude Coupling Metrics.
papers.abstract: Whether emotional processing difficulties in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) stem from deficits in recognizing emotional stimuli or from limitations in flexibly reorganizing brain networks under increasing cognitive demands remains an open question. To our knowledge, this study is among the first to investigate the effects of graded attentional load (low/moderate/high) on EEG-based functional connectivity and brain network organization during task-irrelevant emotional prosody processing in children with high autistic traits (n = 31), by integrating phase-based (iPLV, wPLI) and amplitude-based (AEC) metrics together with graph-theoretic indices within a unified analytic framework. Connectivity matrices from a sliding-window approach were decomposed into edge-level, distributional, and graph-theoretic features and load-dependent changes in connectivity were assessed with statistical analyzes and classification models. The results suggested that attentional load did not uniformly increase or decrease connectivity but rather produced a multi-layered pattern of reorganization that varied as a function of frequency band, connectivity metric, and network topology. Phase-based connectivity in the beta band was decreased with increasing load, while amplitude envelope coupling (AEC) in the theta and alpha bands was increased under high load. This dual-mechanism pattern was most pronounced under the high-load condition, which yielded the greatest number of nominally significant features (uncorrected p<0.05; none survived FDR correction), the largest theta-AEC effect size (Kendall's W up to 0.22), and the best-performing classification model among those tested (accuracy = 72.6%, F1 = 0.725, AUC = 0.764). In conclusion, this exploratory study suggests that, in children with high autistic traits, increasing cognitive demands may be associated with band-specific network reorganization characterized by attenuated phase-based coordination alongside enhanced amplitude-based coupling; these patterns did not survive correction for multiple comparisons, have not been compared with those of typically developed children, and should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. If replicated, such findings could eventually inform how environmental stimulation and cognitive load are structured in special education settings.

papers.title: Dual orexin receptor antagonism modulates sleep during nicotine withdrawal in female and male C57BL/6J mice.
papers.abstract: Sleep disruption is a common symptom of nicotine withdrawal that contributes to relapse risk and impedes successful cessation. The orexin (hypocretin) system regulates sleep-wake states and is implicated in nicotine dependence, making it a candidate target for treating withdrawal-related sleep disturbance. This study tested whether the dual orexin receptor antagonist suvorexant modulates sleep during nicotine abstinence in female and male C57BL/6 J mice. Adult female and male C57BL/6 J mice received nicotine or saline via osmotic mini-pumps for 12 days, after which pumps were removed to induce withdrawal. Sleep-wake behavior was monitored continuously using a noninvasive piezoelectric system. During early abstinence (days 1-2), mice received suvorexant (30 mg/kg) or vehicle at light onset, and outcomes included percent sleep, total sleep time, and sleep-bout architecture (bout frequency and duration) across light and dark periods. Nicotine abstinence altered sleep across multiple metrics, with distinct patterns observed in females and males. In females on abstinence day 2, suvorexant altered early post-dose percent sleep in a nicotine-history-dependent manner, increasing sleep in nicotine-abstinent females. In males, abstinence increased total sleep and bout frequency (fragmentation), indicating a dissociation between sleep quantity and quality, and suvorexant produced only minimal effects. Together, these findings identify nicotine abstinence as the primary driver of sleep disruption and demonstrate that dual orexin receptor antagonism can acutely modulate sleep during nicotine withdrawal, while broader effects on sleep amount and sleep-bout architecture require further investigation.

papers.title: NeuroTest: a benchtop testbed for evaluating sensing-capable electrophysiology and neurostimulation systems.
papers.abstract: The development of increasingly complex implantable neuromodulation devices requires extensive benchtop validation and testing prior to in vivo implementation. Our goal is to enable this in vitro testing by creating a benchtop system that is accessible, easy-to-use, and functions reliably across academic and industry environments, reducing discordant results that arise from discordant approaches. Furthermore, such a system paves the way for standardizing benchtop characterization of future implantable systems by establishing a repeatable and comparable methodology for validating these devices and their capabilities. Approach. We describe the NeuroTest Board (NTB), a low-cost, open-source device that combines a low-noise current source waveform generator with a high-precision data acquisition system. We provide information on its architecture, operation, and performance as an initial benchmark of the potential capabilities of the system. Main results. We demonstrate the use of the NTB to assess electrophysiology systems in two separate applications. In one case, we assess a commonly used laboratory system (the RHD2132 headstage and Open Ephys data acquisition system), while the second case characterizes an investigational neuromodulation device in development for human use (the CorTec Brain InterChange). Following this initial sensing characterization, we explore stimulation-related artifacts that would hamper in vivo data collection. With the NTB, we develop and evaluate artifact mitigation strategies for each system, thus demonstrating an example application of this benchtop testbed. Significance. The ability to test neuromodulation devices against a common benchmark will enable faster development of novel therapeutics by increasing inter-institutional reliability and decreasing troubleshooting time.

papers.title: Transformer networks are robust learners of source localization for EEG measurements.
papers.abstract: EEG source localization is an ill-posed inverse problem complicated by measurement noise, electrode dropout from sensor miscalibration, and variability in the number of active sources. Classical methods such as eLORETA and LCMV beamforming impose regularization assumptions that degrade under realistic noise conditions and do not naturally extend to multi-source scenarios. Recent neural network approaches improve localization accuracy but are typically trained and evaluated under idealized conditions that limit their applicability to real-world EEG acquisition. This work aims to develop and evaluate a source localization model that generalizes across the noise levels, source counts, and electrode configurations encountered in clinical and experimental EEG settings.Approach: We present a transformer-based model for single- and multi-source EEG localization. Hundreds of thousands of simulated EEG measurements are generated from known source locations, spanning a range of noise levels, source counts, and electrode dropout configurations, to train and evaluate the model. We establish a systematic evaluation framework that explicitly factors in source region density, signal-to-noise ratio, and electrode availability, and benchmark the transformer against classical (eLORETA, LCMV beamforming) and deep learning baselines across these conditions. We additionally conduct a thorough ablation study on network architecture and training pipeline design.Main results: Across all tested conditions, the transformer consistently outperforms classical and deep learning approaches, with improvements as high as 12\,mm in mean localization error (MLE) for multi-source scenarios under high noise. Additionally, when number of sources is unknown, the transformer can correctly predict the number and location of sources and drastically out perform the threshold-based approach (e.g an F1 Score of 68\% vs 12\% when simulated at 25\% noise). The multiembedding transformers maintains reasonable performance under conditions such as electrode dropout and increased noise.Significance: By explicitly modeling the noise, electrode dropout, and multi-source variability that characterize real EEG acquisition, this work addresses a key gap between benchmark performance and experimental utility in EEG source localization. These results lay the groundwork for more robust localization techniques applicable to real EEG data, with potential relevance to applications such as brain-computer interfaces. The data and code for this work will be made publicly available to support further development and benchmarking in the field.

papers.title: Force-Torque Classification of Reference-Profile-Defined Drilling States During Robot-Assisted Dental Implant Osteotomy.
papers.abstract: To evaluate whether force-torque features can classify three predefined, reference-profile-defined operational drilling states during robot-assisted implant osteotomy under specimen-level separation.Materials and Methods: Thirty porcine hemimandibular specimens underwent 180 robot-controlled osteotomies under three drilling conditions. Axial force (Fz) and drilling torque (Mz) were sampled at 1000 Hz, segmented into 100-ms windows with a 50-ms step, and represented by 42 time-, frequency-, and wavelet-domain features; 23 features were selected using training-only ANOVA ranking and correlation pruning. Specimens were separated into training, validation, and held-out test sets (18/6/6). Linear support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost were evaluated against predefined depth-indexed operational reference profiles; a same-acquisition CBCT rule served as an imaging comparator.Results: The dataset contained 92,675 overlapping windows. On six held-out specimens (36 osteotomies; 18,496 windows), XGBoost achieved 93.0% accuracy (specimen-clustered 95% CI, 92.0-94.0%), 82.9% balanced accuracy, and 85.6% macro-F1. RF and SVM accuracies were 90.5% and 88.8%, respectively. The CBCT rule achieved 92.3% accuracy but lower balanced accuracy (80.1%) and transitional recall (51.1%). XGBoost transitional recall was 59.6%, increasing to 73.0% in a weighted sensitivity configuration at the cost of lower overall accuracy. Accuracy decreased from 94.1% away from class boundaries to 75.6% in boundary-adjacent windows.Conclusion: Force-torque features differentiated the three predefined reference-profile-defined drilling states under specimen-separated evaluation. XGBoost achieved the highest classification performance, with errors concentrated primarily in transitional and boundary-adjacent windows.Keywords: robot-assisted implant osteotomy; force-torque sensing; reference-profile classification; drilling-state classification; XGBoost; specimen-level validation&#xD.

papers.title: Training Free Signal Enhancement by Random Sampling for Steady State Visual Evoked Potential BCI.
papers.abstract: The steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) is widely used forelectroencephalography (EEG)based brain computer interfaces (BCIs).In order to determine the target commands for SSVEP-BCIs,deep neural networks have been widely used.However, learning-based approaches require training data, and the upfront costs are high.This study proposes a training free signal enhancement method for SSVEP-BCIs.The proposed method enhances SSVEP components by repeatedly performing random sampling andpasting of EEG signals.Our experiments using synthesized signals and open benchmark datasetsdemonstrate the performance of the proposed method.The proposed method outperforms conventional methods for all signal lengths,demonstrating an improvement in information transfer rate of up to 11.30 bit/min.&#xD.

papers.title: Microbial inositol phosphates orchestrate host diurnal metabolism and energy homeostasis via HDAC3.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota programs mammalian circadian metabolism, yet the mechanisms remain unclear. Because feeding behavior is inherently rhythmic and strongly influences microbial metabolism, we hypothesized that the microbiota translates feeding timing into host circadian programs. We show that gut commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (Bt), in concert with feeding schedules, promotes diurnal chromatin-binding activity of the histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) in intestinal epithelial cells. Bt produces inositol triphosphate (InsP3) in a feeding-entrained diurnal manner that enhances HDAC3 activity. Colonization with wild-type Bt, but not an inositol phosphatase mutant, enhanced genome-wide rhythms in epithelial histone acetylation and metabolic gene expression. InsP3-activated HDAC3 deacetylates the transcriptional coactivator PGC-1α, resulting in enhanced expression of nutrient transporter genes. This Bt-InsPs-HDAC3 axis worsens diet-induced obesity in overnourished mice while improving growth in undernourished juvenile mice. These findings reveal a co-evolved microbial-epigenetic-circadian axis that orchestrates nutrient absorption and impacts energy homeostasis across nutritional states.

papers.title: Intraoperative electrocorticography-guided resection of epileptogenic cavernomas: our strategy and literature review.
papers.abstract: Intraoperative electrocorticography (ECoG) in the resection of cavernomas associated with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) has traditionally been performed with strip/grid electrodes for superficial cortical recording. However, there is no evidence demonstrating a better epileptological outcome for ECoG-guided corticectomy beyond the hemosiderin ring compared with resection limited to the hemosiderin ring. The authors describe a new surgical strategy for intraoperative ECoG recording that combines surface strip ECoG (sECoG) with the intraoperative use of a stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) electrode to enable recording of deep areas, such as mesial temporal regions, during resection. The authors conducted a retrospective study of a prospectively collected surgical series of cavernoma-related epilepsy (CRE) cases resistant to antiseizure medications treated surgically at their center. They evaluated the seizure outcome after ECoG-guided tailored resection for the treatment of CRE, and they performed multivariate analysis and proportion comparisons to assess which techniques were associated with better seizure outcomes. A systematic literature review of intraoperative ECoG-guided resection for treating CRE was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Twenty-three patients with supratentorial cavernomas associated with DRE who underwent surgery at their center between September 2020 and May 2024 were selected. The postoperative follow-up was conducted at least 12 months after the procedure. Engel class IA outcomes were achieved in 100% of patients who underwent extension of the lesionectomy to areas identified with the SEEG electrode and sECoG. In the multivariate analysis, SEEG electrode application was the only variable statistically associated with better seizure outcomes (Engel class IA). The authors included 12 studies in the systematic review. Based on the authors' preliminary experience, the combined SEEG electrode/sECoG technique enables a good seizure outcome for the treatment of CRE. Moreover, compared with sECoG, the use of SEEG electrodes was found to be associated with improved seizure outcomes.

papers.title: Association of Altered Anteriorization of Electroencephalographic Alpha Oscillation During Transition to Unconsciousness With Postoperative Delirium: A Prospective Observational Study.
papers.abstract: During sevoflurane-induced anesthesia, electroencephalography analysis demonstrates alpha oscillations shifting from the occipital to the frontal regions, with further characteristic changes during maintenance and emergence. We aimed to exploratorily investigate whether alterations in alpha anteriorization and functional network efficiency are associated with postoperative delirium. This prospective, exploratory observational study enrolled 100 patients from a single tertiary university hospital. Patients were classified into nondelirium (n = 81) and delirium (n = 19) groups based on delirium assessments. After excluding 17 patients due to artifacts on electroencephalography, 19-channel electroencephalography data were collected from 83 elderly patients under sevoflurane-induced anesthesia. Artifact-free epochs were extracted during the induction, maintenance, emergence, and postanesthesia care unit phases. Spectral, topographical, and network analyses were conducted. Postoperative delirium was assessed using confusion assessment method for intensive care unit and a chart review. Significant group differences emerged just before the loss of responsiveness, with the nondelirium group exhibiting robust alpha power amplification across all brain regions (median [interquartile range {IQR}] in dB; frontal: 4.24 [1.86-6.57] vs -0.88 [-1.59-3.38], P = .007; parietal: 3.71 [0.51-5.55] vs -0.95 [-2.33-1.11], P = .046; occipital: 2.81 [0.49-5.71] vs -0.04 [-2.06-1.27], P = .048), whereas the delirium group showed minimal changes. During the maintenance phase, spectral analysis revealed higher alpha power in the nondelirium group across all 19 channels (frontal: 5.42 [2.90-8.16] vs 2.89 [-0.03-5.09], P = .007; 18 of 19 channels significant by false-discovery-rate (FDR)-corrected permutation test). Network analysis demonstrated longer averaged characteristic path lengths in the delirium group (mean ± standard deviation [SD], 4.49 ± 0.62 vs 3.57 ± 0.16, P = .026, FDR-corrected), consistently in the frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, suggesting reduced network efficiency. Delirium was associated with early disruption of alpha anteriorization during induction and globally reduced functional network efficiency during maintenance. Perioperative electroencephalogram (EEG) transition features may serve as early markers of delirium susceptibility.

papers.title: Menopause and Neurology: Clinical Essentials.
papers.abstract: Menopause is a neurobiological transition with important implications for neurologic care. This review summarizes the physiology and hormonal changes of spontaneous menopause and its treatment as applied to cognition, epilepsy, migraine, multiple sclerosis (MS), and stroke. It aims to serve as a resource for neurologists when managing patients in this transitional life stage. Hormonal shifts associated with menopause, particularly declining estrogen and fluctuating estrogen-to-progesterone ratios, influence symptoms, disease expression, and treatment across multiple neurologic conditions. Perimenopause is often associated with subjective cognitive complaints, in part attributed to hypoestrogenism, along with secondary effects from sleep disturbance, vasomotor symptoms, and mood changes. Cognitive symptoms are often transient and rarely with objective neuropsychological deficits or progression. In epilepsy, menopause-related endogenous and exogenous hormones may influence seizure susceptibility and alter antiseizure medication metabolism. Migraine may worsen during perimenopause, especially in estrogen-sensitive phenotypes, with postmenopause stabilization once hormones plateau. In MS, perimenopause and postmenopause contribute to overlapping age-related and MS-related symptoms and is a period of high clinical need with potential acceleration in disability progression despite reduced relapse rate. Ischemic stroke risk rises sharply in postmenopausal women driven by advancing age, accumulation of cardiometabolic risk, and loss of estrogen's protective effects. Oral estrogen-containing systemic menopause hormone therapy (MHT) is associated with increased thromboembolic events (including stroke), whereas transdermal regimens seem safer and are preferred at low or standard doses (≤50 mcg estradiol patch or ≤1.5 mg [or 2 pumps] per day of 0.06% estradiol gel). Timing of initiation also modulates this risk and plays a critical role with a favorable risk:benefit window when initiated in women younger than 60 years or within 10 years of menopause onset. Neurologists should routinely consider reproductive history, menopausal stage, symptom burden, and disease risk factors when evaluating midlife and older female patients. When appropriately selected, MHT can be safely used in many neurologic populations, with nonoral routes for estrogen and nonhormonal options generally preferred. Incorporating menopausal considerations into neurologic practice offers an important opportunity to optimize care and advance precision medicine.

papers.title: Is psychomotor retardation a sixth domain of negative symptoms?
papers.abstract: The five canonical domains of negative symptoms in schizophrenia - blunted affect, alogia, asociality, anhedonia, and avolition - were established by a consensus process. Meta-analyses have placed psychomotor retardation (PMR) rating scale items in negative symptom factors, suggesting it may be a sixth negative symptom domain. We pooled data from two cross-sectional, multicenter, international studies of schizophrenia (N = 271) and used PANSS item G7 (Motor Retardation) as a measure of PMR. In multivariate analyses we examined G7 as a predictor of cognitive function, personal and social function, and negative symptoms other than PMR. We also examined whether G7 mediated the association between extrapyramidal symptoms and negative symptoms. In some analyses the G7 factor had relationships characteristic of the five canonical domains: correlations with those negative symptoms and negative correlations with function and cognition. However, other findings were consistent with its classification as a motor symptom: significant correlations with the PANSS Mannerism and Posturing item and with extrapyramidal symptoms, and mediation of the relationship between extrapyramidal symptoms and the canonical negative symptoms. There was no significant relationship with self-reported hours of sleep. PMR showed associations with negative symptoms, cognitive impairment, and functional outcome, consistent with status as a sixth negative symptom domain. However, other findings leave unclear whether it should be considered a negative symptom, a motor symptom, or something more complex. Problems in the G7 item definition and description contribute to this uncertainty.

papers.title: Gamma-band network segregation links corollary discharge dysfunction and anomalous self-experiences in schizophrenia.
papers.abstract: Anomalous self-experiences (ASEs) are a core feature of psychotic disorders and reflect disturbances in ipseity. Impairments in corollary discharge mechanism have been proposed as a neurobiological substrate of ASEs, and an imbalance between brain network integration and segregation, may impair the coherent flow of mental contents, thereby disrupting their fluid and implicit character. However, the relationship between corollary discharge and functional network properties has not been directly examined. This link was assessed in thirty participants with schizophrenia and thirty healthy controls. Functional network was computed using the Phase Locking Value (PLV) from resting-state EEG in the gamma band and two parameters were calculated: the clustering coefficient (ClC, as a proxy for segregation) and the path length (PL, as a proxy for integration); corollary discharge was indexed by N1 suppression in a talk-listen paradigm; and ASEs were evaluated using the 'Inventory of Psychotic-Like Anomalous Self-Experiences' (IPASE) total score. Patients with schizophrenia showed significantly greater gamma-band network segregation and lower integration than healthy controls. Moreover, higher segregation in this band was associated with reduced N1 suppression and greater ASEs severity in patients, whereas network integration was not associated with N1 suppression nor ASEs. These findings suggest that excessive gamma-band network segregation may be correlated with disrupted corollary discharge functioning and may compromise the distinction between self-generated and external stimuli. Therefore, it may alter the sense of ipseity by interfering with the integration of mental contents into the flow of consciousness, thereby contributing to greater severity of ASEs.

papers.title: Noninvasive respiratory therapy: A physiology-oriented approach across acute, chronic, home, and palliative care settings.
papers.abstract: Noninvasive respiratory therapy has evolved from a strategy used to avoid endotracheal intubation in selected forms of acute respiratory failure into a broader framework encompassing acute care, chronic respiratory failure, sleep-disordered breathing, home respiratory support, pulmonary rehabilitation, and palliative care. The term now encompasses conventional oxygen therapy, high-flow nasal cannula therapy, continuous positive airway pressure, bilevel noninvasive ventilation, home noninvasive ventilation, home high-flow therapy, and positive airway pressure therapy for sleep-related breathing disorders. This review proposes a physiology-oriented approach. Rather than selecting a device solely according to the disease, clinicians should identify the dominant physiological problem: impaired oxygenation, alveolar hypoventilation, upper-airway obstruction, increased work of breathing, respiratory muscle fatigue, impaired secretion clearance, or the need for comfort-oriented support. In acute care, noninvasive ventilation is well established for acute hypercapnic respiratory failure due to COPD exacerbations and for acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema, whereas high-flow nasal cannula therapy, continuous positive airway pressure, and noninvasive ventilation require more careful selection in patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure. In chronic care, home noninvasive ventilation and home high-flow therapy should be understood as components of long-term respiratory care systems rather than as simple device prescriptions. Practical success depends on appropriate interface selection, leak control, humidification, patient-device synchrony, airway clearance, patient education, and safe monitoring. A physiology-oriented and patient-centered framework may improve the appropriate use of noninvasive respiratory therapy across the continuum of care.

papers.title: Bridging the gap: Are OSA patients ready for Telemedicine? An Italian perspective.
papers.abstract: Different telemedicine approaches for managing sleep disorders have been extensively researched worldwide, yet data on patients' individual willingness to adopt these protocols remain limited. This study aims to fill this gap, focusing specifically on the Italian population. A 19-item anonymous questionnaire was administered to 255 consecutive obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) patients. Our findings indicate a substantial willingness to use telemedicine: 56.5% were unreservedly in favour of remote follow-up and 67.4% preferred comprehensive telemonitoring to PAP-only monitoring, although only 48.6% were familiar with the term "telemedicine". Attitudes towards remote consultations were more nuanced: 51.8% were unreservedly in favour, but within a combined model with telemonitoring only 40.6% would also accept them, and 45.7% considered in-person consultations irreplaceable. The need for assistance increased with age and, in multinomial logistic regression, older age was the main determinant of both refusal and perceived obstacles (odds ratios per age class 2.1-2.9), whereas educational level was not significantly associated with the response pattern after adjustment. Privacy concerns were frequent: 38.0% reported doubts or concerns, including 14.9% who were unwilling to transmit their data electronically, a response that, in exploratory analyses, was more frequent among more educated patients. Most patients (90.8%) believed that telemedicine services should be provided by the Public Health Service. In conclusion, telemedicine may be well received by Italian patients with OSA as a complement to, rather than a replacement of, in-person care; its implementation should consider public funding, tailored digital support for older patients, and robust data governance and privacy safeguards.

papers.title: DCDA-Net: A depthwise convolution dilated attention network with temporal weighted loss for seizure prediction.
papers.abstract: The sudden and unforeseeable nature of seizures poses serious threats to patients' safety and quality of daily life, making the development of highly accurate and reliable seizure prediction methods of significant clinical importance. To this end, this study proposed a seizure prediction model by integrating depthwise convolution and a novel dilated attention mechanism, named DCDA-Net. Depthwise convolution was first employed to extract features from each EEG channel independently, preserving spatial channel information for subsequent seizure evolution analysis. Innovatively combining dilated convolution with self-attention mechanisms, a dilated attention module was devised to efficiently capture long-range temporal dependencies. Furthermore, a temporal weighted loss function was introduced to significantly enhance the model's ability to discriminate critical preictal temporal features. Validation results on the CHB-MIT and SH-SDU clinical databases demonstrated that the model achieved a segment-based accuracy of 97.56% and an event-based sensitivity of 97.69% with a false prediction rate of 0.0232/hour on the CHB-MIT database, while attaining a segment-based accuracy of 96.93% and an event-based sensitivity of 96.05% on the SH-SDU database. Additionally, channel importance analysis confirmed significant spatial consistency with the actual epileptogenic zones. This study offered an efficient solution for patient-specific seizure prediction, with substantial potential for further clinical assessment.
papers.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society

papers.title: Examining the effectiveness of theory-based nursing interventions for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS): A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The aim of this systematic review was to evaluate the effectiveness of theory-based nursing interventions for individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS). A comprehensive search of the PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and Cochrane databases was performed to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between January 1, 2015, and May 1, 2025. Following a rigorous screening process in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, nine studies meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were included in the review. The included studies evaluated interventions grounded in nursing theories, including Orem's Self-Care Model (n = 3), the Continuous Care Model (n = 3), Pender's Health Promotion Model (n = 1), the Theory of Goal Attainment (n = 1), and the Collaborative Care Model (n = 1). The findings indicate that the application of these theory-based nursing interventions were associated with statistically significant improvements across multiple outcomes, including quality of life, self-efficacy, activities of daily living, treatment adherence, hope, fatigue, stress regulation, lifestyle modification, and sleep quality. Most studies exhibited high methodological quality. Theory-based nursing interventions not only yield significant positive effects on physical, psychological, and behavioral outcomes among individuals with multiple sclerosis but also serve as an essential framework for guiding the planning and delivery of holistic nursing care.

papers.title: Adult aphasic status epilepticus: A systematic review and patient-level synthesis of clinical phenotypes and multimodal diagnostic evidence.
papers.abstract: Aphasic status epilepticus (ASE) is an uncommon manifestation of focal status epilepticus in which aphasia is the sole or predominant clinical feature. Recognition may be difficult because consciousness can be relatively preserved, convulsive activity may be absent, and the presentation can mimic acute stroke.
