To characterize diagnostic phenotypes of adult ASE and synthesize clinical, electrographic, and neuroimaging features across published cases. We conducted a systematic review and patient-level synthesis of adult ASE cases. Eligible patients were adjudicated as definite or probable ASE using prespecified criteria. Clinical phenotype, electroencephalographic (EEG) findings, neuroimaging, initial diagnostic impressions, treatment, and language outcomes were extracted. Ninety-nine publications contributed 168 adults with ASE, including 89 definite and 79 probable cases. Aphasia was the sole manifestation in 42.9% and predominant in 57.1%, while consciousness was preserved in 78.0%. Ictal EEG activity or electrographic status epilepticus was documented in 53.0%, and 41.7% had supportive epileptiform abnormalities. Among cases with interpretable EEG laterality, 92.7% were left-lateralized. Peri-ictal MRI abnormalities occurred in 41.2% of performed interpretable studies. Among 55 patients with interpretable functional perfusion or metabolic imaging, hyperperfusion was reported in 32. FDG-PET hypermetabolism was treated as a distinct metabolic finding. Stroke or transient ischemic attack was the most frequent reported initial impression (44.2%). Complete language recovery was reported in 77.4% of evaluable patients. Published adult ASE cases show a heterogeneous phenotype in which recognition commonly rests on concordance between language disturbance and focal EEG abnormalities, with peri-ictal imaging providing complementary evidence. These findings do not establish diagnostic accuracy of individual features or multimodal combinations.

papers.title: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) in quality of epilepsy care: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: The current lack of an unambiguous and widely applicable quality indicator for epilepsy care could hamper epilepsy care. The main aim of this systematic review is to study patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) instruments that evaluate the quality of epilepsy care and inventorize the main themes covered as well as the measurement properties of these instruments. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (ID: CRD42025637902) and reporting followed the PRISMA reporting guidelines for systematic reviews. Electronic databases searches were conducted on PubMed, Embase and Web of Science. Articles published up to 2025 were considered. Dutch or English-language articles with a focus on the development and validation of PROMs to evaluate epilepsy care were included. Reviews, editorials, conference abstracts, protocols and translations were excluded. Covered themes and measuring properties (validity, external reliability, internal reliability and readability) were extracted. Risk of bias assessment was performed using 'Consensus-based Standards for the selection of health measurement instruments' (COSMIN) guidelines. The search resulted in 1,904 articles. Seven articles met our inclusion criteria, evaluating a total of seven instruments. Recurring themes included seizure control (n = 5), treatment (n = 5), daily life (n = 3), psychosocial functioning (n = 3). Less frequently addressed themes included diagnostics (n = 2), quality of life (n = 2), injury (n = 2), reproductive health (n = 1), sleep (n = 1) and informal caring (n = 1). Most instruments evaluating epilepsy care focus on seizure control and treatment aspects while other domains like daily activities and psychological functioning are less well covered. Including these domains is however advisable as they are important components of QoL.

papers.title: Selected red blood cell folate measures are associated with lower odds of insufficient sleep in United States adults.
papers.abstract: Insufficient sleep has been linked to diet, but its relation to longer term folate status is unclear. We hypothesized that red blood cell (RBC) folate measures would be inversely associated with insufficient sleep. We analyzed 4224 adults aged ≥20 years from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021-2023, including 836 with insufficient sleep. Insufficient sleep was defined as a weekday/weekend weighted mean sleep duration <7 h/night. Survey-weighted logistic regression accounted for the complex sampling design. The weighted prevalence of insufficient sleep was 19.2%. In the primary model, each 1-standard deviation higher concentration was associated with lower odds of insufficient sleep for conventional RBC folate (odds ratio, 0.865; 95% confidence interval, 0.777-0.963), total washed RBC folate (0.847; 0.746-0.962), washed RBC 5-methyltetrahydrofolate (0.853; 0.764-0.953), and MeFox (0.842; 0.761-0.930); THF and 5,10-methenylTHF were not associated with the outcome. Estimates changed little after adjustment for day 1 energy intake, dietary folate equivalents, and supplement use. Restricted cubic spline models showed no evidence of nonlinearity. Model-standardized prevalence was 20.3% in the lowest and 15.2% in the highest quartile of total washed RBC folate. Results were similar in sensitivity analyses, including additional adjustment for serum cotinine. These cross-sectional findings are consistent with inverse associations for selected RBC folate measures but do not establish temporal direction or a benefit of folate supplementation.
keywords: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey

papers.title: Recurrence analysis of cardiac arrhythmias: A systematic review of methods, substrate characterisation and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias are a major cause of morbidity and mortality, and catheter ablation depends on accurate identification of the underlying substrate. Cardiac signals are nonlinear and non-stationary, which limits Fourier-based analysis. Recurrence quantification analysis (RQA) and related recurrence methods make fewer assumptions, but their use in arrhythmia research has not been systematically synthesised. This review examines what recurrence analysis has demonstrated, how consistently its methods have been applied, and what remains before it can support clinical substrate characterisation. Of 309 records retrieved from four databases (207 after deduplication), 48 studies met the eligibility criteria and citation searching added one, giving 49. Each study was examined in full text for its signals, cohorts, embedding parameters, threshold selection, metrics and results, and assigned to one of six methodological categories. The three studies that tested recurrence against surrogate or shuffled data each found structure in fibrillatory signals that matched stochastic surrogates did not reproduce. Recurrence metrics and dominant frequency were weakly correlated and diverged in substrate characterisation, so they are not interchangeable. Threshold selection was the most consequential uncontrolled variable: five strategies were in use, ten of the 35 studies that apply a threshold reported no selection rule, and only three examined how their results depended on it. Determinism and laminarity, although the most frequently reported metrics, were not consistently the strongest discriminators. Clinical readiness is not established: only one study used recurrence mapping prospectively to guide ablation, in ten patients without randomisation. A shared threshold-selection standard and prospective multicentre validation are needed.

papers.title: Neural circuitry mediating hypercapnia-induced microarousal and impaired sleep depth.
papers.abstract: Sleep disruption in obstructive sleep apnea syndrome is characterized by frequent microarousals and reduced sleep depth, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that intermittent hypercapnic air (HA) induces time-locked microarousals, fragments sleep, reduces non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep depth, and diminishes rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. HA exposure activates glutamatergic neurons in the nucleus tract solitary (NTSVglut2), and their optogenetic or chemogenetic activation is sufficient to trigger arousal and impair sleep. Projection-specific activation reveals that NTSVglut2 projections to the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), parabrachial nucleus (PB), paraventricular thalamus, and locus coeruleus (LC) promote arousal, whereas projections to the PB and LC additionally reduce NREM sleep depth. Inhibition of NTSVglut2 projection to the PVN significantly postpones HA-induced arousal. NTSVglut2 terminals monosynaptically activate corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons in the PVN (PVNCRH), and inhibition of PVNCRH neurons or knockdown of Slc17a6 (encoding Vglut2), but not Crh, delays hypercapnia-induced arousal. These findings identify neural circuits underlying hypercapnia-induced microarousal and reduced sleep depth.

papers.title: Factors Associated With Overweight and Obesity Among Adolescents in South Asia: A Narrative Review of Recent Evidence.
papers.abstract: Adolescent overweight and obesity are increasing across South Asia, contributing to diabetes and other noncommunicable diseases. Previous reviews have examined prevalence and selected associated factors, but evidence remains heterogeneous across countries, populations and adiposity definitions. This narrative review synthesised recent evidence on prevalence and factors associated with overweight and obesity among South Asian adolescents. We conducted a structured narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. PubMed, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched for peer-reviewed studies published from January 2015 to March 2025, supplemented by targeted searches through August 2026. Studies of adolescents aged 10-19 years and predominantly adolescent populations with overlapping age ranges were considered. Primary studies and evidence syntheses were analysed separately. Methodological quality was evaluated using design-appropriate Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal checklists, and findings were synthesised narratively. Thirteen publications were included: eight primary studies and five systematic reviews or meta-analyses. Prevalence varied by population, setting, adiposity measure and classification system. Regional meta-analytic estimates were 12.4% for overweight, 6.6% for obesity and 19.3% for combined overweight/obesity, although these were not directly comparable with adolescent-specific primary studies. More consistent evidence concerned physical inactivity, sedentary behaviour and unhealthy dietary practices. Associations with socioeconomic position, urban residence, sex and gender, familial factors and media exposure were more limited and context dependent. Sleep, mental health, food insecurity and neighbourhood environments were insufficiently examined. Most primary evidence was cross-sectional and school based. Adolescent overweight and obesity in South Asia are associated with behavioural, dietary and socio-environmental factors within changing food and urban environments. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneous definitions, uneven country coverage and predominantly cross-sectional designs. Standardised population-based and longitudinal studies, including out-of-school adolescents, are needed to guide context-specific prevention.

papers.title: Decoding motor imagery EEG signals by a deep learning network integrating multiscale filtering and temporal-channel attention mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Due to their low signal-to-noise ratio and non-stationarity, accurately classifying EEG signals is still one of the main hindrances that limit the real-world applications of a brain-computer interface (BCI). Deep learning (DL) is a potential method for addressing the problem. However, how to create a suitable DL network for motor imagery (MI)-based BCIs poses severe challenges in the case of insufficient training data. In this paper, a DL network based on multiscale convolutional neural network (CNN) and temporal and channel attention mechanisms is proposed for decoding MI tasks. Temporal and spatial features are extracted by four parallel CNN branches, each of which is followed by a Transformer block for learning the global correlations of local time features. The outputs from the four Transformer blocks are concatenated along channel dimension and then input into a channel attention module for channel fusion. The subsequent feature map is classified by a CNN, which replaces the commonly used fully connected layer for reducing computational complexity. The proposed network was evaluated on three publicly available BCI datasets and compared with five state-of-the-art DL networks. The training data sets are augmented using the approach segmentation and reconstruction. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network achieved an average accuracy of 80.21% on Dataset 1 (4-class tasks), 90.19% on Dataset 2 (2-class tasks), and 97.32% on Dataset 3 (4-class tasks), surpassing the strongest baselines FBCNet on Dataset 1, MSFBCNN on Dataset 2 and MSFBCNN on Dataset 3 by 2.59%, 1.27%, and 1.99% respectively. The network effectively decoded the MI-based EEG signals, providing a potential method for BCI applications.

papers.title: Robust acoustic representation of Japanese vowels under phonation variability using dynamic spectral analysis.
papers.abstract: Phonation-induced acoustic variability, particularly in whispered speech, poses persistent challenges for stable vowel representation. Conventional static formant-based descriptors often fail to capture the dynamic spectral behavior of vowels under such conditions. This study evaluates the robustness of acoustic feature representations for Japanese vowels across normal and whispered phonation, comparing static formant measures with dynamic spectral features derived from Vowel Inherent Spectral Change (VISC). Dynamic features are used to characterize continuous formant trajectory patterns, while Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest (RF) classifiers serve as analytical probes to assess representation stability rather than as targets of algorithmic optimization. Results demonstrate that incorporating dynamic spectral information leads to more consistent vowel discrimination across phonation types compared to static-only representations, with similar performance trends observed across classification frameworks. These findings suggest that differences in classification outcomes are primarily driven by properties of the acoustic representations rather than by model choice. The study highlights the im-portance of representation-level design for robust speech signal analysis under phonation-induced variability and supports the use of low-dimensional dynamic features for vowel modeling in variable phonation conditions.

papers.title: Beyond sleep duration: nighttime glucose in gestational diabetes mellitus.
Anti-Freezing, Conductive Triple-Network Hydrogel for Wearable Sensing and Stable Biopotential Recording over 24 Hours.
papers.abstract: Hydrogel-based sensors face two persistent challenges: freeze-induced performance failure at sub-zero temperatures and an inherent trade-off between mechanical robustness and electrical conductivity. To address these issues, a triple-network hydrogel composed of polyacrylamide, gelatin, and carboxymethyl cellulose was designed, synergistically integrated with LiCl, CaCl2, and glycerol. In this design, glycerol serves as the primary cryoprotectant, Li+ ions provide ionic conduction, and Ca2+ crosslinks reinforce the polymer network. The optimized hydrogel achieves high tensile strength (576 kPa), ultra-high stretchability (938%), outstanding toughness (233.4 kJ/m3), and high conductivity (2.95 S/m), while completely suppressing ice crystallization down to -80 °C. As a strain sensor, it delivers a gauge factor of 3.53 after freezing; as a bioelectrode, it records high-quality EMG, ECG, EOG, and EEG signals comparable to or surpassing commercial Ag/AgCl electrodes, and maintains reliable performance over 24 h at -20 °C. This work demonstrates a durable material candidate for long-term wearable sensing and biopotential recording in sub-zero environments.

papers.title: Home non-invasive ventilation in chronic respiratory failure: Evidence-based guidelines.
papers.abstract: Home non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is used across a range of causes of chronic respiratory failure, but patient selection and management are disease-specific. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations on initiating, titrating, and monitoring long-term home NIV across different disease spectrums. The panel reviewed studies from international databases, relevant guidelines, and reference lists. The panel refined recommendations through two rounds of consensus and graded them using the Indian Chest Society framework. In chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), home NIV is recommended for eligible patients with persistent daytime hypercapnia, including those who remain hypercapnic 2 to 4 weeks after an exacerbation. High-intensity bilevel ventilation should be titrated to achieve a meaningful reduction in arterial carbon dioxide. In neuromuscular disorders, respiratory muscle weakness or hypoventilation warrants timely assessment for NIV, alongside evaluation of interface tolerance and secretion clearance. For stable obesity hypoventilation syndrome with severe obstructive sleep apnoea, continuous positive airway pressure is generally the preferred initial treatment; NIV is appropriate when severe obstructive sleep apnoea is absent or continuous positive airway pressure fails or is not tolerated. The guidelines also address heart failure with sleep-disordered breathing, chest-wall deformity, interstitial lung disease, bronchiectasis, post-tuberculosis lung disease, central hypoventilation syndromes, and palliative care. Across indications, management should include individualised ventilator settings, objective assessment of ventilation, patient and caregiver education, and structured follow-up. Where evidence is limited, recommendations reflect expert consensus and should be applied in the context of patient goals, clinical feasibility, and available resources.
papers.journal: Lung India : official organ of Indian Chest Society

papers.title: The hidden burden of endoscopy in Saudi Arabia: Burnout, musculoskeletal injury, and emotional impact of complications among endoscopists.
papers.abstract: Endoscopy is central to gastrointestinal care but is associated with significant occupational stressors, including high workload, physical strain, and psychological impact following complications. Data on endoscopist wellbeing in the Middle East remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of burnout, musculoskeletal symptoms, and emotional consequences of complications among endoscopists in Saudi Arabia. A national cross-sectional survey was conducted between October and November 2025 among licensed endoscopists across Saudi Arabia. The questionnaire assessed demographic characteristics, workload, musculoskeletal symptoms, burnout indicators, complication experience, emotional impact, and institutional support. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. A total of 76 endoscopists participated. High workload was common, with 73.7% performing ≥20 procedures per week and 78.9% working ≥41 hours weekly. Musculoskeletal symptoms were reported by 64.5% (49/76). Burnout-related indicators included frequent fatigue (28.9%) and emotional exhaustion (17.1%). Working ≥41 hours per week was independently associated with frequent fatigue. A significant complication was reported by 64.5%, with psychological effects including sleep disturbance (56.6%), intrusive thoughts (27.6%), and loss of confidence (35.5%). Avoidance of similar procedures occurred in 35.5%, while 60.5% reported no formal debriefing or institutional support. Endoscopists in Saudi Arabia experience a substantial physical and psychological burden, compounded by limited institutional support. Targeted interventions, including ergonomic training, structured debriefing, and peer-support programs, are needed to improve clinician wellbeing and sustain endoscopy services.
papers.journal: Saudi journal of gastroenterology : official journal of the Saudi Gastroenterology Association

papers.title: Domain-Tailored Attention Transformer for EEG-Based Person Identification.
papers.abstract: Accurate person identification (PI) based on electroencephalogram (EEG) provides high security value. However, existing EEG-based PI methods still struggle to fully mine individual-specific features within each do main and to effectively jointly model multi-domain information, which limits identification performance. To address these limitations, we propose the Domain-Tailored Attention Transformer (DTAT) model, which designs tailored attention modules for each domain to thoroughly mine individual-specific features, thereby enabling effective joint modeling across multiple domains. Specifically, in the spatial domain, to address the neglect of high-frequency spatial variations, we introduce a Discrete Cosine Trans form (DCT)-informed Spatial Attention (DSA) module. DSA transforms spatial EEG maps into the frequency domain and aggregates full-band components from global structures to local textures, enabling fine-grained characterization of individual-specific spatial patterns. For the temporal domain, to remedy the oversight of salient amplitude variations, we propose an Amplitude-aware Temporal Attention (ATA) module that jointly models global activation trends and localized amplitude fluctuations, adaptively emphasizing time steps with prominent amplitude responses to encode identity-critical transient temporal sig natures. To overcome the overlooking of uneven frequency band contributions in spectral modeling, we develop an Adaptive Spectral Attention (ASA) module that models localized spectral dependencies and dynamically recalibrates band-wise importance, thereby selectively enhancing identity-relevant spectral features. These three domain tailored attention modules work collaboratively to fully extract individual-specific representations from EEG signals thereby improving PI performance. Extensive experiments show the superiority of DTAT over state-of-the-art methods on multiple EEG datasets. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DTAT-79D6.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: DINO-EEG: Montage-Robust Event-Level Seizure Detection in Scalp EEG.
papers.abstract: Manual review of long-term clinical electroencephalography (EEG) remains a major bottleneck for large-scale seizure screening in intensive care and epilepsy monitoring settings. Most automated seizure detection methods formulate this task as epoch-level classification, which does not directly provide clinically relevant event boundaries. In addition, many existing systems are sensitive to montage configuration and channel availability, which limits their use in routine clinical practice. We present DINO-EEG, a channel- wise framework for event-level seizure detection in scalp EEG. The method processes each EEG channel independently and directly predicts seizure onset and offset using an object-detection formulation, after which channel- wise detections are aggregated into global seizure events. This design targets two practical goals: direct event-level output and improved robustness to variability in electrode configuration. On the Temple University Hospital EEG Seizure Corpus (TUSZ) v2.0.3, evaluated under the event-based SzCORE (Seizure Community Open-Source Research Evaluation) framework, DINO-EEG achieved an event-based F1 score of 0.641, with a mean sensitivity of 0.663 at 12.5 false positives per 24 hours (FPs/24 h) in seizure subjects, while yielding 4.7 FPs/24 h in seizure-free subjects. The method also remained stable under mild-to-moderate channel dropout and retained seizure detection capability during direct transfer to the CHB-MIT and Siena datasets without retraining. These results suggest that channel- wise event detection is a practical and clinically aligned strategy for automated seizure detection in retrospective EEG review workflows.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: Effect of Acupuncture for Loss of Appetite in Advanced Lung Cancer Undergoing Immunotherapy: Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BackgroundLoss of appetite (LOA) is a highly prevalent and distressing symptom in advanced lung cancer, leading to malnutrition, poorer treatment tolerance, and reduced quality of life. Although acupuncture may help manage cancer-related symptoms, its effect on LOA in patients receiving immunotherapy is unclear. This study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for alleviating LOA in this population.MethodsThis multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial will enroll 80 eligible patients with advanced lung cancer undergoing immunotherapy who experience LOA, defined as a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) score ≥30 mm. Participants will be randomly assigned to either true acupuncture or sham acupuncture in a 1:1 ratio, administered over 24 sessions within a 12-week period. The primary outcome is the LOA response rate at week 12. Secondary outcomes include changes in LOA severity, nutritional and hematologic markers, patient-reported measures (appetite/cachexia, disease symptoms, psychological distress, and sleep), and tumor response. Safety and blinding success will also be assessed. Data will be analyzed using SPSS 20.0 and R software.DiscussionTo our knowledge, this is the first rigorously designed trial evaluating acupuncture for LOA in advanced lung cancer patients undergoing immunotherapy. The findings may inform integrative supportive care strategies for this patient population.

papers.title: Exploratory data analysis and machine learning-based assessment of social media addiction and its impact on academic performance and mental health among students.
papers.abstract: This study investigates social media addiction among students. It includes definitions, ways to measure it, how common it is, and its effects on mental health and academic performance. A focused review of literature from 2018 to 2025 gathers systematic reviews, meta-analyses, psychometric studies, and research that connects problematic social media use to issues like mental health problems, sleep disruptions, and academic results. The article also provides a method for analyzing student-level social media addiction data. It discusses common findings in datasets and offers recommendations for educators and policymakers based on evidence. Using data from 705 participants across 110 countries, this study combines a thorough literature review, dataset-driven exploratory data analysis (EDA), and correlational modeling. The results show strong connections between social media addiction, academic success, sleep, and mental health. The EDA reveals gender differences in usage, regional differences in platform preferences, and clear links between addiction and poorer sleep quality and mental health. These findings align with global research and suggest the potential value of targeted digital well-being interventions among students.

papers.title: Cell-type dependence of effects from transcranial electric brain stimulation.
papers.abstract: There is an urgent need for better treatment options for many neurological conditions, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, depression, and epilepsy. Transcranial electrical stimulation (tES) is a non-invasive, safe, inexpensive, and promising method that could address some of this unmet need. The therapeutic value of tES has been well demonstrated, but the effect is highly variable. To enable tES to reach its full potential requires a better understanding of how tES modulates neural activity so that tES treatments can be tailored to specific neurological conditions and individual patients. The neural response to tES is, however, highly complex, and the parameter space involved in optimizing tES treatments is daunting. This has made it difficult to obtain general insights into how tES modulates neural activity, and a central challenge lies in the cell-type-specific and frequency-dependent nature of these responses. In this study, we investigated cell-type-specific neuronal responses to tES over a broad frequency range, using a large database of biophysically detailed neuron models. We found that pyramidal cells respond strongly to low-frequency tES, but their responses drop sharply with frequency. In contrast, inhibitory neurons show a smaller reduction and, on average, become more responsive than pyramidal cells above ~60 Hz. By leveraging a reciprocity theorem we demonstrated that the effect of tES on a given cell-type is proportional to the frequency-dependent current-dipole moment that determines the EEG-signal contribution of this cell-type. We further identified the dendritic asymmetry as key in determining tES responses across the frequency spectrum. Counterintuitively, we also found that while total cell length increases tES sensitivity at low frequencies, it can have the opposite effect at high frequencies. Furthermore, we derived an analytical formula for idealized neuron models which can approximately predict the tES sensitivity of different cell types at any given frequency. By characterizing the role of morphology and stimulation frequency in determining tES responses of single cells, this is an important step towards a better understanding of tES at the fundamental level. These results also provide an efficient and accurate method for characterizing and comparing the tES responses of different neural populations across the frequency spectrum, which facilitates optimizing tES for cell-type specific targeting.

papers.title: Association among Dietary Inflammatory Index, sleep quality and nutritional status in fixed daytime and rotating shift workers.
papers.abstract: Shift work is associated with irregular eating behaviors, increased energy intake, and impaired sleep quality. Poor dietary patterns may elevate systemic inflammation, contributing to long-term metabolic and cardiovascular risks. The aim of this study was to investigate differences in the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII), sleep quality, dietary intake, and anthropometric and body composition measures between fixed daytime workers and rotating shift workers and to examine the associations among these parameters. This cross-sectional study included 52 male workers employed at a defense industry factory in Ankara, Türkiye, who worked either fixed daytime or rotating shifts. Dietary intake was assessed using 24-h dietary recalls for three non-consecutive days, from which macronutrient and micronutrient intakes were calculated. DII scores were computed to assess the inflammatory potential of the diet. Sleep quality was evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Anthropometric measurements, body composition, blood pressure, and biochemical parameters, including fasting plasma glucose, lipid profile (total cholesterol, HDL-C, LDL-C, and triglycerides), C-reactive protein, and homocysteine, were measured using standardised protocols. Rotating shift workers had significantly higher total energy intake and higher daily intakes of fructose, total fat, saturated and monounsaturated fatty acids, cholesterol, and several micronutrients, including vitamin A, folate, iron, calcium, and phosphorus compared with fixed daytime workers (p < 0.05). Mean DII scores did not differ significantly between the groups (Fixed daytime: 0.2 ± 1.86; rotating shift: -0.2 ± 2.25). DII scores were positively correlated with global PSQI score (r = 0.278, p = 0.046), the PSQI sleep duration component score (r = 0.319, p = 0.021), and daytime dysfunction component score (r = 0.287, p = 0.039); however, the association between DII and overall sleep quality was no longer statistically significant after adjustment for potential confounding factors (age, BMI, smoking status, physical activity, and work schedule). These findings suggest that dietary habits, pro-inflammatory dietary patterns, and poor sleep quality may represent co-existing factors associated with metabolic risk, and addressing these factors may contribute to better overall metabolic health.

papers.title: Neuropharmacology of language: ERP evidence for catecholaminergic modulation of syntactic processing.
papers.abstract: A few studies have shown that brain catecholamines are implicated in language comprehension. However, the specific cognitive processes they modulate remain underexplored. We hypothesized that catecholamines enhance the unification of syntactic roles and word meanings into coherent multiword structures. This study combined electroencephalography and psychopharmacology to examine the effects of a catecholaminergic stimulant (methylphenidate) on processing sentences containing local syntactic ambiguities. Methylphenidate amplified the P600 event-related potential effect, which has been linked to the recruitment of cognitive resources for processing sentences with increased syntactic load. The drug's impact on semantic processing was subtler, showing a suggestive attenuation of the N400 effect to ambiguous sentences. Furthermore, the increase in the P600 effect under methylphenidate was most pronounced in participants with lower working memory capacity. This study provides evidence for linking catecholamine activity to syntactic unification in healthy individuals. Elevated catecholamine levels appear to increase the cognitive effort invested in syntactic unification, and to support the dynamic prioritization of syntactic information when contextual demands require it.

papers.title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides.
papers.abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

papers.title: Relationship Between Objective Measures of Sleep and Nocturnal Cardiovascular Physiology and Swimming Performance in Collegiate Female Athletes: A Bayesian Analysis.
papers.abstract: Vatne, EA, Cencer, D, Vatne, M, Pulvermacher, K, Saenz, C, Kraemer, WJ, Robinson, B, Jones, P, Quebedeaux, N, Sprague, R, Dial, M, Carpenter, T, and Hagen, J. Relationship between objective measures of sleep and nocturnal cardiovascular physiology and swimming performance in collegiate female athletes: A Bayesian analysis. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-There is substantial evidence that sleep influences athletic performance; however, relationships with real-world competition outcomes remain unclear. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to explore the associations between objectively measured sleep, nocturnal cardiovascular physiology on the night before competition, and swim performance in female collegiate athletes. Female swimmers (n = 11) who wore a sleep monitoring device the night before competition, competed in the 200-yard freestyle (short course yard), and had ≥21 of 28 prior nights of valid data were included. Sleep metrics included total sleep time (TST), time in bed (TiB), and sleep efficiency (SE), whereas nocturnal cardiovascular metrics included heart rate variability (HRV) and resting heart rate (RHR) standardized as individualized z-scores. Race times were obtained from a publicly available database. Bayesian linear mixed-effects models estimated posterior probabilities of performance improvement. Results indicated a high probability that greater TST and TiB were associated with faster race times, with substantial support for improvements of at least 1 second per additional hour of sleep. In contrast, SE, HRV, and RHR showed low posterior evidence of meaningful associations with performance. These findings extend prior sleep and performance literature that has been confined to proxy assessments of athletic performance in controlled settings to real-world competition that should inform athlete education, emphasizing the importance of sufficient sleep opportunity and duration before competition.

papers.title: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface.
papers.abstract: Brain activation to verbal commands can be detected by EEG in clinically unresponsive patients. These patients with cognitive motor dissociation (CMD) are unable to communicate with the environment despite preserved consciousness. Advanced brain-computer interfaces (BCI) are promising to support motor function in patients with motor neuron disease or spinal cord injury. Our primary objective was to determine if clinically unresponsive patients can control a self-paced, one-way BCI early after acute brain injury. Secondarily, we assessed the association of BCI control with short- and long-term outcomes. We conducted a prospective single-centre cohort study in 41 clinically unresponsive, critically ill and acutely brain injured patients, as well as in a convenience sample of 8 healthy volunteers and 22 conscious critically ill patients. The self-paced BCI analysed EEG in real time and modulated frequency and pitch of a tone that patients controlled by attempting a motor task: patients were provided with instructions 'to make the beep sound faster, keep opening and closing your right hand' alternating with 'to make the beep sound slower, stop opening and closing your right hand'. CMD was detected by applying machine learning to EEG recorded while patients listened to motor commands. Clinical outcomes were recovery of consciousness by hospital discharge, assessed with the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised, and recovery of functional independence at 12 months, defined as a Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended score of 4 or higher (denoting the ability to function independently for 8 h or more). Additionally, we invited conscious patients as well as family members of conscious and clinically unresponsive patients to complete a survey on perceived utility and challenges associated with the BCI. In this study, 13 clinically unresponsive patients (32%) achieved BCI control and 8 of 41 (20%) were CMD-positive. All healthy volunteers and nine conscious patients (41%) were able to control the BCI. Median signal delay for BCI control was 49.8 [interquartile range (IQR) 39.9-75.6] seconds for clinically unresponsive patients, 17.1 (IQR 7.8-19.9) for conscious patients and 15.5 (IQR 12.9-21.2) for healthy volunteers. In the group of 41 clinically unresponsive patients, 4 of 13 patients with (31%) and 1 of 28 without BCI control (4%) recovered clinical consciousness at hospital discharge [odds ratio (OR) 21.2; 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.3-930.7]. At 12 months, 6 of 13 patients with (46%) and 2 of 28 without BCI control (7%) recovered functional independence (OR 9.9; 95% CI 1.8-81.6). None of the patients that were unable to control the BCI and were CMD-negative recovered. Patients with BCI control had shorter times to recovery of functional independence by 12 months than those who did not (hazards ratio 6.0; 95% CI 1.2-30.6). All respondents of the BCI survey (n = 37) expressed strong support for the potential future use of BCI devices. These results suggest that BCI control is a strong predictor of outcomes following acute brain injury and provide initial evidence that a bedside, EEG-based BCI system might permit bidirectional communication in critically ill unresponsive patients.

papers.title: InFACT: Bridging Visual Variance With Semantic Invariance Via Informed Adapter Tuning for Cross-Subject Video Seizure Detection.
papers.abstract: Timely seizure detection is vital for patient intervention. Video-based approaches offer a non-contact, patient-friendly alternative to traditional EEG monitoring. However, their effectiveness is fundamentally hindered by the significant visual variance of seizure behaviors both within and across patients. While existing methods attempt to mitigate this via complex feature extraction, they struggle to eliminate the impact of variance, particularly under drastic appearance shifts caused by complex poses or environmental clutter. Crucially, we observe that although pixel-level appearances fluctuate, the clinical semantics of seizure actions can remain invariant across patients sharing similar semiological patterns. To this end, we propose InFACT (Informed Fusion Adapter with Consistent Text), a dual-branch framework that treats text as a semantic anchor to calibrate visual representations. Specifically, an Informed Fusion Adapter fine-tunes a VideoMAE, a pretrained video masked autoencoder, specializing generic motion priors into seizure-specific pathological patterns under textual guidance. Simultaneously, a Consistency-aware Text Encoder extracts stable behavioral descriptions from a Multimodal Large Language Model, filtering out task-irrelevant visual noise. Furthermore, a cross-modal contrastive learning mechanism aligns divergent visual features with these invariant semantic anchors, ensuring tight clustering of seizure classes regardless of patient identity. Experimental evaluations show that InFACT achieves 86.1% sensitivity, 89.6% specificity on the public SAH-ZU dataset, and 94.3% sensitivity, 96.5% specificity on our in-house FAH-USTC dataset, yielding consistent performance improvements over state-of-the-art methods and proving its robustness against cross-subject variability.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

papers.title: A Molecular Communication Channel Model for Early Epileptic Seizure Detection via Synaptic Glutamate Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Molecular communication (MC) is a bio-inspired paradigm that models information transfer through molecules and provides an approach to analyze biological processes. Positioning neurological signaling within this framework enables a communication-theoretic view of disorders such as epilepsy. Epileptic seizures originate from microscopic neurotransmitter dynamics. Current prediction methods rely on EEG, which captures only macroscopic activity and often misses early preictal buildup. We propose an MC framework that models microscale synaptic glutamate signaling as a channel shaped by diffusion, clearance, and finite-receptor binding. Our Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) and Chemical Master Equation (CME) combined model yields impulse response and validates stochastic binding. Further analysis shows how synaptic parameters influence detection dynamics. Framing seizure prediction as a threshold-crossing detection problem aligns with latency and reliability metrics in communication theory, positioning MC as a promising framework for next-generation molecular-level seizure detection.

papers.title: Multimodal Analysis of Brain Network Abnormalities in Autism Spectrum Disorder: a Graph Neural Network-based Fusion Investigation of EEG and fNIRS.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify brain network abnormalities of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) by analyzing multimodal neuroimaging data through graph neural networks (GNNs), laying a technical foundation for future machine learning-based neuroimaging analysis. We employed combined electroencephalogram (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to capture brain activity of 58 ASD children and 63 age- and gender-matched typically developing (TD) children. The concurrent EEG and fNIRS data were fused using an enhanced GNN to identify ASD with high accuracy. Key connections and regions of interest (ROIs) were identified for each group, followed by graph theory metrics (e.g., local efficiency) and topological data analysis (TDA) to quantify group differences. The proposed GNN model achieved 84% accuracy, outperforming the single-modality approach. Analysis of subgraph created by the model showed that the two groups exhibited different neural patterns in motor-language integration and lateralization, a key basis for GNN models to distinguish between the two groups. Individuals with ASD may also have topological defects such as lower average local efficiency and a lack of high-order structures. The proposed framework effectively captures quantitative insights ranging from specific connection-level variations to network-level differences, identifying candidate discriminative connectivity patterns within this cohort. This study establishes a multimodal deep learning framework that identifies candidate discriminative topological signatures from fused EEG-fNIRS data, providing preliminary within-cohort classification evidence and an exploratory topological analysis framework.

papers.title: Social jetlag and alcohol use in adolescents: A random-intercept cross-lagged panel analysis.
papers.abstract: Alcohol use and social jetlag (i.e., the misalignment between weekday and weekend sleep timing) frequently co-occur during adolescence, yet their temporal dynamics across different timescales remain underexamined. This study assessed bidirectional relationships between alcohol consumption and social jetlag at the person, 4-month, and weekly levels. U.S. high school students (N = 302, analytic n = 297; Mage = 16.21 years) completed three 21-day assessment bursts, each comprising three consecutive weekly surveys and timeline follow-back assessments. Bursts were separated by 4 months and spanned approximately 9 months. A three-level random-intercept cross-lagged panel model disaggregated variance into person-level (stable differences), burst-level (medium-term shifts), and week-level (short-term fluctuations) components. At the person level, the random intercepts for social jetlag and alcohol use were positively correlated (β = .42). At the burst level, Burst 1 alcohol use positively predicted alcohol use in Burst 2 (β = .26), whereas alcohol use in Burst 2 negatively predicted alcohol use in Burst 3 (β = -.41). At the week level, a cross-lagged effect emerged in Burst 3: Greater alcohol use predicted greater social jetlag the following week (β = .40). Results suggest that associations between adolescent alcohol use and social jetlag differed across temporal levels. A stable between-person association emerged, whereas within-person directional associations were inconsistent across timescales and bursts. One weekly association from alcohol use to social jetlag emerged in the third burst only and should be interpreted cautiously pending replication. These findings highlight the value of distinguishing stable co-occurrence from short-term within-person dynamics in adolescent sleep-alcohol research.
